artifact: resolved.json — entity resolution and lineage independence over four blind discovery beats
standing_caveat: EVERY claim in this file is V0-UNRESOLVED. Not one citation carried here was resolved to bytes by any agent in this sweep. Outbound egress blocked .gov/.mil and most archive hosts; the beats worked from search-result summaries and snippets throughout. Where a source is described, that is evidence that a SUMMARY exists, not evidence of the document's contents. This resolution pass adds no evidence of any kind — it only rearranges what four agents already reported, and it can therefore only ever LOWER confidence, never raise it.
independence_rule_applied: Two beats reporting the same candidate is NOT corroboration. Four agents searched the same indexed web blind to one another; a claim found twice is one source surfaced twice. The fan-out improved RECALL and contributed nothing to corroboration. No independent-origin count in this file was incremented because two beats agreed. Where beats agreed, the count was left alone; where they disagreed, both readings are recorded and the one supported by sources actually held was carried.

counts.counting_note: 'independent origins' counts origins surviving the default-SAME rule and the access test and bearing on the candidate's OWN headline propositions. Sub-claim counts are listed separately and deliberately NOT added in: RES-026's four institutional roots attest the Los Alamos subterrene RESEARCH PROGRAMME, not the claimed tunnel network; RES-027's three roots attest the 1934 EPISODE, not the Lizard People city; RES-034's two roots attest the REX 84 PLANNING, not the claimed underground camps. Adding them in is exactly the laundering this register exists to prevent.

Both beats that discussed its method concluded it works from public property records, i.e. it is probably a DERIVATIVE of the historic-preservation and land-records layer rather than an independent terminus. Under the default-SAME rule it collapses into whatever record it worked from.

candidates.verification_state: V0-UNRESOLVED — every source behind this record is SEARCH-SNIPPET-ONLY, FETCH-BLOCKED or CITED-BY-OTHERS-NOT-SEEN. No citation in this file has been resolved to bytes by any agent.
candidates.mundane_alternative: A08 — an ordinary earth-bermed or partially below-grade federal office building of late-1960s design on a large federal campus, whose Cold War name reflects the agency that happened to occupy it rather than any protective engineering. This null is genuinely strong: the Denver Federal Center is a sprawling multi-building campus assembled from a wartime ordnance plant, and it contains a great deal of unremarkable government construction. What would distinguish it: the NRHP nomination's statement of significance, or the USACE design record, specifying a design overpressure, blast closures, shielding or CBR filtration. What would NOT distinguish it: earth cover, reinforced concrete, absence of windows, a generator, or the building's Cold War-era name.
candidates.claim_origin: Not a folklore claim and there is no fringe origin to trace — this is an administratively named federal property. The earliest traceable appearance in the material reaching me is institutional rather than popular: the National Register listing dated 16 December 1999, which would have been preceded by a nomination prepared by or for the property's federal custodian. Popular circulation appears to postdate and derive from that institutional record and from the Center for Land Use Interpretation's early-2000s survey, not the reverse. This is the inverse of the usual pattern in this register and it is why the candidate is worth prioritising.
candidates.expected_records: For a 1969 USACE-designed facility on a federal campus for an appropriated civil-defence agency, the records that SHOULD exist are: a construction appropriation or MILCON-equivalent line (X3 for an appropriated agency in this era); USACE design and as-built drawings in RG 77 (X1, flagged ARCHIVE-GAP — roughly 96% of NARA textual holdings are undigitised); a GSA real-property record (X2); and the NRHP nomination form (X3 — NRHP nominations for non-restricted properties are systematically public and their absence WOULD be surprising). The NRHP nomination is the single most valuable expected record here precisely because its absence would be informative, which is rare in this beat. All returned UNSEARCHED, not NEGATIVE.
candidates.confidence_note: Highest-priority candidate in this beat, and the one I would verify first. Reason: it is the only entry here whose decisive document is a public, indexed, machine-resolvable form (an NRHP nomination) rather than a classified or undigitised record. It is therefore the cheapest possible test of whether this beat can produce a band-A proposition at all. If the register cannot verify Building 710, it cannot verify anything on this beat.

propositions.statement: A substantial earth-covered subsurface federal structure designated Building 710 exists on the Denver Federal Center campus.
propositions.assessment: Multiple independent-looking channels describe the structure, and critically it is described as listed on the National Register of Historic Places, which if true means a nomination form exists in a public register with a physical description on its face. That is a document class that states the proposition explicitly and whose issuing authority (the Keeper of the National Register, via the Colorado SHPO) has authority over the fact of listing. I resolved none of it. Verification debt: if the NRHP nomination resolves at the National Register or at History Colorado, EXIST would plausibly reach A via BES 3.4; on today's record it is X.
propositions.proposed_band: X — VERIFICATION PENDING (SCI≈0, V=∅; ceiling if the NRHP nomination resolves: A)

undercutting: None found. I note that I searched for undercutting evidence and found none, which given SCI≈0 is uninformative rather than reassuring.
propositions.diagnosticity_note: An NRHP listing record discriminates strongly IF its statement of significance describes the structure as a hardened operations centre, because the ordinary-federal-office null does not produce a Cold War Defense Structure listing. But the diagnosticity lives entirely in text I have not read. The bare fact 'a building exists on a federal campus' is D0.

propositions.statement: Building 710 was engineered to survive the effects of nuclear attack beyond ordinary construction for a 1960s federal office building.
propositions.assessment: Search summaries attribute to GSA and History Colorado the statements that the building was 'designed specifically to withstand a nuclear attack' and 'constructed of reinforced concrete, except for interior partition walls', and was 'designed and constructed by the United States Army Corps of Engineers'. If GSA's own page says that, GSA is the custodial agency and has authority over the fact for its own building, which would be a BES 3.4 gate candidate. I have not seen the page. Note also that 'reinforced concrete with metal-stud partitions' is not by itself a hardening specification — it describes most institutional construction of the period — and no overpressure rating, blast-door specification or design standard reached me. Verification debt: A if the GSA/NRHP text states protective engineering on its face; B if it asserts survivability without specification.
propositions.proposed_band: X — VERIFICATION PENDING (ceiling if GSA/NRHP text resolves: A)
supporting: Reported GSA historic-buildings text describing design to withstand nuclear attack (search snippet only)
Reported USACE as designer and constructor (search snippet only)
Reported earth cover of approximately three feet (search snippet only)
undercutting: The only construction detail that reached me — reinforced concrete with metal-stud interior partitions — is not diagnostic of hardening and is equally consistent with the mundane alternative.
propositions.diagnosticity_note: Discriminating: a stated design overpressure, a blast-door or blast-valve line item, a CBR filtration specification, or a USACE design memorandum citing a protective-construction standard. NOT discriminating and present here: earth cover, reinforced concrete, being windowless, being on a federal campus. Earth-bermed and partially buried construction was a common 1960s energy and siting choice and appears on the BES universal-D0 list in substance.

propositions.statement: The structure served as the Defense Civil Preparedness Agency Region 6 emergency operations centre and subsequently as the FEMA Region 8 operations centre.
propositions.assessment: The function is carried in the building's own registered historic name, which is a strong form of claim-property evidence because a naming authority recorded the function for its own unrelated purpose. It also fits the independently arriving eight-region administrative enumeration, in which Denver is Region 6 under OCDM/OCD/DCPA. The renumbering to FEMA Region 8 in 1979 is a real trap: 'Region 6' in a pre-1979 document and 'Region 6' in a post-1979 document are different places (post-1979 Region 6 is Denton, Texas), and any register entry that merges them on the region number alone is committing an entity-resolution error.
propositions.proposed_band: X — VERIFICATION PENDING (ceiling if the NRHP name and nomination resolve: A)
supporting: The registered property name itself, as reported by History Colorado (search snippet only)
Independent administrative enumeration placing Denver as OCDM/DCPA Region 6 (search snippet only, attributed to NARA Guide to Federal Records)
propositions.diagnosticity_note: The registered historic name is claim-property evidence of an unusual kind: a naming authority recorded the function for its own preservation purpose, unrelated to any bunker claim, which is the BES 5.1.7 access test being satisfied. NOT discriminating: FEMA's current occupancy, which is equally predicted by the null that an ordinary federal building was later assigned to a regional office.

propositions.statement: As of the most recent reporting reaching me, the facility remains in federal use as a FEMA regional operations centre.
propositions.assessment: Reported as current, but 'current' in a search summary can be years stale and FEMA's regional footprint has been under active reorganisation pressure. Not established.

candidates.mundane_alternative: A10 — a federal office building whose below-grade levels carry a civil-defence fallout-shelter designation and nothing more, with 'bunker' being a local honorific applied to an ordinary basement. This null is weakened, though not excluded, by the 13-ton door: fallout-shelter designation required shielding mass, not blast closures, and licensed shelter space in ordinary basements was enormously common. What would distinguish it: the door's engineering rating, or an OCD construction contract as opposed to an OCD shelter-survey licence. What would NOT distinguish it: being underground, thick walls, ventilation equipment, a generator, or a shelter sign.
candidates.claim_origin: No fringe origin. Earliest traceable appearance in the reaching material is institutional and contemporaneous — the facility opened publicly in 1964 as a named federal installation and was never concealed. Modern circulation has two visible nodes, neither of which invented the claim: the Center for Land Use Interpretation's site survey, and the 2017 Harvey news cycle in which FEMA itself invited cameras inside. The civildefensemuseum.com virtual tour appears to be independent of both and works from period civil-defence material.
candidates.expected_records: For 1964 construction by an appropriated civil-defence agency: an appropriation or construction line (X3 — its absence WOULD be surprising for this agency and era); GSA real-property and, latterly, FRPP entries (X2); a Denton County deed for the parcel (X3, the universal floor); USACE or agency design records (X1, ARCHIVE-GAP); local building permits (X0 — federal construction on federal land does not permit locally). Chronicling America coverage of 1964 local press is X0 because the free corpus is copyright-bounded after 1963, which is an unlucky boundary for exactly this facility and pushes the local-press check to newspapers.com or NewsBank. All UNSEARCHED.
candidates.confidence_note: Existence is not seriously in doubt on any reading; this is a publicly acknowledged, currently operating, camera-toured federal facility. The live propositions are HARDEN (specifically, whether the one-megaton figure has a documentary parent) and the 'first in the nation' priority claim. Second verification priority after Building 710.

propositions.statement: A two-level subsurface federal structure exists at Denton, Texas, opened in 1964.
propositions.assessment: The most broadly attested facility in this set, including through channels that imply direct physical access: national and regional broadcast journalism covering FEMA's Hurricane Harvey response from inside it (2017), a Denton County government history-office article (2024), and a civil defence museum virtual tour. Journalists filming inside a facility are, in principle, resolvable direct observers under BES A1-alt, though I have no georeferenced imagery matched to a control point and no named observer resolvable in a record predating the claim. Verification debt: plausibly A via A1-alt or via a GSA/FEMA real-property record; today X.

propositions.statement: The facility was engineered against nuclear blast effects, including a rated blast door and a stated design overpressure.
propositions.assessment: This is the most specific hardening claim reaching me anywhere on this beat: a 13-ton blast door, air scrubbers, and a design criterion stated as surviving a one-megaton detonation at one mile. A stated design criterion is qualitatively different from 'hardened' as an adjective and is the kind of assertion that traces to an engineering document. But it reached me through popular journalism and a county history blog, not through the engineering record, and a figure of this shape is exactly the sort that propagates unchanged across copies while losing its provenance. The 13-ton door is a physical object a visitor can see and describe; the one-megaton-at-one-mile figure is not, and the two should not be graded together.
propositions.proposed_band: X — VERIFICATION PENDING (ceiling if the design criterion is traced to a construction record: A; if only visitor description of the door survives: B)

undercutting: No design standard, contract or drawing is named in any source reaching me. The overpressure figure is quoted without attribution in every instance I saw.
propositions.diagnosticity_note: The blast door is diagnostic and discriminates cleanly: an ordinary federal office basement does not have a 13-ton rated door, and the named null cannot produce one. The unit cost is weakly diagnostic — $2.7M in 1964 for 50,000 sq ft is high for ordinary office construction and would become properly diagnostic if checked against a period cost-per-square-foot norm for the building class, which is a concrete verification task. The air scrubbers are diagnostic for CBR filtration. Earth cover and being underground are D0.

Reported capacity of about 500 federal employees. The 1979 renumbering to FEMA Region 6 is the same entity-resolution trap flagged at Denver and cuts in the opposite direction.

propositions.statement: The Office of Civil Defense and Mobilization planned purpose-built hardened regional centres for all eight of its civil-defence regions, and Denton was the first constructed.

The 'first in the nation' priority claim is a distinctive assertion that either is or is not in the construction record, and it is the kind of claim local boosters generate spontaneously — I would test it before repeating it. The eight-region programme claim is independently supported by the administrative enumeration. Note that PROGRAM carries no physical claim about any individual site and is clamp-exempt under BES 1.4.

propositions.statement: The facility was hardened against attack effects.

A converted naval munitions magazine is inherently a heavy reinforced-concrete earth-covered structure — that is what magazines are — but magazine design protects the outside world from the contents, not the contents from a weapon, and the two are not the same engineering problem. Converting a magazine yields blast resistance almost incidentally and yields essentially no attack-specific protection (no CBR filtration, no shock isolation, no EMP treatment) unless it was deliberately added.

Its origin is specific and traceable: a blog maintained by and about White House Communications Agency personnel, describing facilities its author's community operated. A self-published blog satisfies none of the custody conditions as it stands, however genuine the author. The architectural detail — pie-shaped rooms in an annulus around a tower base — is distinctive and internally coherent, which is a mild positive signal and also exactly what makes the claim propagate.

The reported $170 million repair bill is the signature of an ageing conventional building, not a protected one. A converted sanitarium is close to the least survivable structure a continuity agency could occupy.

candidates.name: AT&T Long Lines "Project Office" chain — five hardened mid-Atlantic troposcatter stations

merged_from.name: AT&T Long Lines "Project Office" chain — five hardened mid-Atlantic troposcatter stations

candidates.era: Built late 1950s to mid-1960s; terminal stations reported in service 1963 (Hagerstown) and 1966 (Chatham); troposcatter links reported out of service by the 2000s; two stations reportedly still AT&T-operated.
candidates.jurisdiction: Multi-state: Washington County MD; Loudoun County VA; Albemarle County VA; Buckingham County VA; Chatham County NC

location.description: A north–south chain of five hardened stations running from the Bear Pond Mountains northwest of Hagerstown, Maryland, through Short Hill Mountain in western Loudoun County, Virginia; Peters Mountain roughly 16 miles east of Charlottesville, Virginia; Spears Mountain roughly 11 miles west of the town of Buckingham, Virginia; to a site off Big Hole Road in Chatham County, North Carolina, south of Chapel Hill.
location.basis: Verbal placement only, taken from search summaries of the CLUI Land Use Database and coldwar-c4i.net. No coordinate was resolved in this session and none is asserted. The landform names above are the strongest locators the sources supply and are sufficient to drive a parcel or HTMC query.

lineage.assessment: TWO for the physical description, ONE for the continuity-of-government function. L1 = LaFrance / coldwar-c4i.net, from which Wikipedia's 'Project Offices' article, the Grokipedia mirror, Wikimapia annotations and most enthusiast restatements descend. L2 = CLUI, whose entries read as independent site visits but whose framing language is close enough to LaFrance's to collapse into L1 under the default. L3 = Elliston / Indy Week 2000, genuinely independent but CHATHAM-ONLY. Kastleman 2020 is a fourth publication, not a fourth lineage.
lineage.collapse_or_note: THE COG FUNCTION CLAIM HAS ONE SOURCE AT ANY VOLUME, and that source states it as hedged conjecture. See CITOGENESIS-02.

candidates.verification_state: V0-UNRESOLVED — every source behind this record is SEARCH-SNIPPET-ONLY, FETCH-BLOCKED or CITED-BY-OTHERS-NOT-SEEN. No citation in this file has been resolved to bytes by any agent.
candidates.mundane_alternative: A07 — a hardened Defense Communications Agency AUTOVON switching and troposcatter relay chain and nothing more: a commercial carrier building military-grade voice plant under DoD contract, hardened because DoD's own specifications required survivable switching, with no sheltering or relocation role for any person. This null accounts for every physical feature reported: earth cover, blast valves, decontamination bay, standby generation, filtered positive-pressure ventilation, elevated physical security, remote siting. WHAT WOULD DISTINGUISH IT: berthing. A switching station houses equipment and a small maintenance crew; a relocation facility houses people. Bunk capacity, galley and messing provisions, potable-water storage sized to a population rather than to a crew, sanitary capacity, and a decontamination bay sized for personnel rather than vehicles all discriminate cleanly. Secondary discriminators: whether the parcel was ever federally leased or subject to a federal restrictive covenant (county deed chain); whether the site carries a federal frequency assignment in the NTIA GMF as well as an FCC licence; whether any DD-1391 or MILCON line names the location. All of these are checkable and none was checked in this sweep.
candidates.claim_origin: Two distinct origins, traced as far as the index allows. (1) THE FACTUAL SKELETON of the chain — five stations, their locations, tropo reflectors, earth-covered buildings, AUTOVON role — traces to Albert LaFrance, a named Virginia researcher, publishing at coldwar-c4i.net ('A Secret Landscape: The Cold War Infrastructure of the Nation's Capital Region'). The site has been running since at least the early 2000s; a 2002-era mailing-list post referencing it appears in the index, which is a usable earliest-appearance anchor but was not receipted. (2) THE COG INTERPRETATION traces to the same source, and — this is the important part — LaFrance states it as inference, in hedged language ('probably not the station's primary mission', 'most likely', 'may have served'). The unhedged form now circulating on Wikipedia, CLUI, Grokipedia, War History Online, OnlyInYourState and dozens of listicles is a downstream hardening of one researcher's stated conjecture. Separately, (3) the CHATHAM-SPECIFIC factual detail (purchase price, construction cost, contractor, square footage, 45-year operating span) traces to Jon Elliston, 'Big Hole, Deep Secret', Indy Week, 13 December 2000 — an independent origin, because Elliston appears to have worked from deed records and local interviews rather than from LaFrance. I could not establish an earlier appearance than 2000 for the Chatham material or than the early 2000s for the chain material, and I did not run the canonical ORIGIN corpora (Wayback CDX, IA full-text, Chronicling America), so no ORIGIN proposition is offered.
candidates.expected_records: For a 1960s programme built by a common carrier under federal contract, here is what SHOULD exist and whether the silence is surprising. COUNTY DEED AND ASSESSOR RECORDS FOR ALL FIVE PARCELS — X3, the universal floor; AT&T bought land in five named counties and those transfers are recorded. Their absence would be genuinely surprising and none has been checked. Elliston's reported $27,000 purchase price for the Chatham tract is exactly the sort of figure that comes out of a deed book, which is a reason to think the record exists and is findable. USGS HTMC TEMPORAL STACK — X3; five 1960s excavations on named landforms should appear, and editorial blanking between editions would itself be D2. FCC ASR/ULS — X3 for the towers as commercial emitters, though note the ASR is authoritative only for the structure and the licence, never for what is under it. NTIA GMF federal assignments — X0; federal spectrum is withheld by aggregation, and its absence carries no information at all. MILCON / DD-1391 — X0 if AT&T financed the buildings on its own capital, which is the ordinary Bell System pattern for Long Lines plant; X3 only if federal construction money flowed, and establishing which of those two worlds we are in is the single highest-value unresolved question on this beat. CREST / DTIC for a facility programme still partly operational — X0. NEPA — X0, predates NEPA entirely. FRPP / GSA disposal — X0, AT&T is not an executive agency. Bell System Practices and AT&T route/plant engineering literature — X2 and the best target: the Long Lines corporate record is partly in private and enthusiast hands and is the class of document that, per the calibration set's Fairview case, carries D3.
candidates.confidence_note: The chain's physical existence I regard as very likely true and well within reach of documentation; a county parcel sweep across five counties would probably settle EXIST at A or B within a day of unblocked access. The COG function I regard as genuinely open and currently ungraded in the strict sense — one researcher's hedged inference, restated confidently by everyone downstream, with a single genuinely diagnostic artefact (the Greenbrier switchboard label) that nobody appears to have pursued properly. The temptation on this beat is to let the chain's obvious realness launder the COG claim onto it. That is the v0.1 unit error and I have deliberately not made it.

propositions.statement: AT&T built, in the late 1950s–1960s, a programme of five nuclear-hardened troposcatter communications stations in the mid-Atlantic, internally referred to as 'Project Offices', whose nature AT&T has never publicly described beyond calling them 'central facilities'.
propositions.assessment: The programme's existence as a named, bounded set is the best-supported thing on this beat. Three sources that do not obviously copy one another — Albert LaFrance's coldwar-c4i.net, the CLUI Land Use Database, and Jon Elliston's 2000 Indy Week reporting — independently describe a small chain of AT&T-built hardened tropo stations, and CLUI and LaFrance agree on the count of five. Nothing I saw is a primary record. Conditional: if a Bell System route/plant document or an AT&T corporate history naming the programme resolves, PROG plausibly reaches B; if only the compilations resolve, PROG is capped at C by CAP-1 because CLUI most likely descends from LaFrance.
supporting: coldwar-c4i.net ATT_Project index — 'Five nuclear-hardened, secure communications stations were built by AT&T in the mid-1960s in sparsely-populated areas of the mid-Atlantic region'
CLUI Land Use Database — Short Hill Mountain entry describes 'one of five similar facilities in the mid-Atlantic region known as Project Offices'
Wikipedia 'Project Offices' — AT&T 'has chosen not to disclose the exact nature of business conducted at Project Offices, describing them only as central facilities'
Elliston, Indy Week, 13 Dec 2000, 'Big Hole, Deep Secret' — investigative reporting on one member of the set
undercutting: No federal primary record naming the programme was found in the general index. Under the ERP table this is near-uninformative (see expected_records), so it is listed as a gap rather than scored as a negative.
AT&T's own refusal to describe the facilities is consistent both with a classified federal mission and with ordinary common-carrier reticence about critical network plant — it does not discriminate.
propositions.proposed_band: X
propositions.diagnosticity_note: A named programme of five stations is not by itself diagnostic of anything beyond 'AT&T built five stations'. What discriminates is the described feature set — earth-covered buildings, drive-through decontamination bays, blast valves, helipads, physical security beyond conventional AT&T practice — none of which a routine microwave relay carries. That feature set is D2-ish IF an instance-level record confirms it. Today it is asserted by compilations only.

propositions.statement: Five substantial earth-covered subsurface structures exist at the five named locations.
propositions.assessment: Scope is CLASS here, not INSTANCE — this proposition is about the set. Per §2.4 class evidence cannot certify any individual hilltop, and the individual site entries below carry their own EXIST. What can be said: multiple independent site-visit-based compilations, at least one peer-reviewed article, at least one investigative newspaper piece, and a county land-use proceeding in which AT&T applied to build ON TOP of an existing underground building, all place substantial subsurface structures at these coordinates. Conditional: individually these would likely reach B–A once county parcel records and USGS HTMC temporal stacks are pulled, because a 1960s excavation of this scale leaves deed, assessment and cartographic traces that are X3 expected records.
supporting: CLUI entries for Short Hill Mountain, Chatham, Peters Mountain Road and Buckingham each describe an underground building
Loudoun County commission permit proceeding 2016 in which AT&T sought to build a 160,000 sq ft aboveground structure adjacent to 'its already-existing underground facility'
coldwar-c4i.net per-site pages describing earth-covered buildings with drive-through entrance-decontamination areas
propositions.proposed_band: X
propositions.diagnosticity_note: A buried building is on the universal-D0 list — limestone mines, sewer works and cold storage all produce one. What lifts it above D0 for this set is not the hole but the drive-through decontamination bay and blast valves, which no mundane alternative for a telephone relay produces. That distinction is exactly why EXIST and HARDEN must be graded apart.

propositions.statement: The Project Offices served a continuity-of-government function beyond their AUTOVON switching role — specifically, sheltering or supporting federal officials in a nuclear emergency.
propositions.assessment: This is the load-bearing claim on the whole beat and it is the weakest. Its origin is a single named researcher's explicitly hedged inference. LaFrance writes, in the summaries I saw, that AUTOVON switching 'was probably not the station's primary mission', that the AUTOVON equipment was 'installed to serve another activity housed at the sites', and that it is 'likely' and 'most likely' that the stations supported a classified COG programme and 'may have served' as a relocation site. Wikipedia, CLUI and the downstream popular press restate the conclusion with the hedges stripped. That is the citogenesis pattern the register exists to name. Conditional: even with full receipts, this cannot exceed E under CAP-2b unless a verified instance-scope CLAIM-PROPERTY record appears, because every current support is either place-property (the building has a helipad) or is the compiler's inference.
supporting: coldwar-c4i.net — hedged inference that the stations supported a classified COG programme
Greenbrier bunker switchboard reportedly labelled 'CHATAM' and 'HGRSTOWN' — a physical artefact inside a declassified, publicly toured federal COG facility naming two members of this chain
Wikipedia 'Project Offices' — restates COG function and links it to the Greenbrier
undercutting: AUTOVON switching alone fully accounts for a hardened, blast-valved, decontamination-equipped telephone building. DoD required its switches to survive; that requirement produces every observed feature without any sheltering function.
Helipads are D0 on the universal list where an aviation or medical justification is absent but a maintenance-access justification is present, which it is for remote mountaintops.
The claim's strongest form ('emergency relocation site for senior executive-branch officials') is asserted by no source I saw as anything other than a possibility.
propositions.proposed_band: X
propositions.diagnosticity_note: This is the sharpest diagnosticity failure on the beat. Every physical signal offered for the COG reading — hardening, decontamination, helipad, security, generators — is REQUIRED by the AUTOVON mission on its own. A signal that both hypotheses predict at equal strength is D0 and contributes nothing at any volume. The Greenbrier switchboard label is the one genuine exception: a COG facility's own equipment naming this chain is improbable if the chain were purely a DoD voice-switching asset with no COG relationship. That single item is worth more than everything else in this row, and it is the item most worth receipting.

propositions.statement: The terminal stations of the chain (Hagerstown and Chatham) housed AUTOVON switching equipment for the Defense Communications Agency.
propositions.assessment: Consistently asserted across LaFrance, Wikipedia and CLUI, and consistent with the documented AUTOVON architecture (switches sited away from population centres, avoidance routing). No primary record seen. Conditional: an FCC ULS/ASR record establishes licensee and path but has authority only over the licence, not over the DoD network role, so it would be D4 for FUNCTION(relay) and no better than D2 for FUNCTION(AUTOVON switch). The record that would settle it is a DCA/DISA network document or a Bell System Practice.
supporting: coldwar-c4i.net — 'The terminal stations contained AUTOVON switches'
Wikipedia 'Project Offices' — AUTOVON in service 1964, Chatham on line 1966
propositions.proposed_band: X
propositions.diagnosticity_note: Discriminates well against A07 'ordinary unhardened telecom exchange': an AUTOVON switch is a documented DoD asset class with a published architecture and published siting doctrine. It discriminates not at all against the COG reading, since AUTOVON and COG are compatible.

propositions.statement: The five stations enumerated here (Hagerstown MD / HGTWMDQ0010; Short Hill Mountain–Leesburg VA / LSBGVA05 / '[VA-1]'; Peters Mountain VA; Spears Mountain, Buckingham County VA; Chatham County NC) are the complete membership of the set the sources call 'Project Offices'.
propositions.assessment: Membership is asserted consistently but the boundary is soft. CLUI's Chatham entry calls Chatham 'the southernmost of four other facilities in the region', LaFrance calls Hagerstown 'the northernmost of five', and Peters Mountain and Buckingham are variously described as 'relay stations' between the Project Offices rather than as Project Offices themselves. Netcong NJ, which some search summaries associated with the group, is a different animal — AT&T's network operations centre, not a tropo station — and I have excluded it. The set is enumerable and closable, which matters: it is the precondition for the §9.2 C1c candidate-set path on any individual member.
supporting: coldwar-c4i.net per-site pages naming Hagerstown as northernmost of five and Buckingham as part of the Project Office chain
CLUI Chatham entry — 'the southernmost of four other facilities in the region known as Project Offices'
undercutting: Terminology is inconsistent across sources: 'Project Office', 'troposcatter relay station' and 'Project Office chain' are used interchangeably, so the set may be a chain of five stations of two different classes rather than five instances of one class.
propositions.proposed_band: X
propositions.diagnosticity_note: Not diagnostic of function; diagnostic of method. A closed set of five with a published denominator is what would let a thin instance be graded via C1c instead of being asserted at large. If the set is really 'two terminals plus three relays', N and M change and every member re-grades.

location.description: On the ridge of Short Hill Mountain in western Loudoun County, Virginia, in the 'Between the Hills' area near Hillsboro and Lovettsville, north of Harpers Ferry.
location.basis: Named landform from CLUI and Loudoun County land-use reporting. No coordinate resolved; the Loudoun County parcel record and the 2016 commission-permit file would both give an exact one and neither was reachable.

lineage.assessment: TWO, and the comms beat says this is the only candidate on which it would assert independence with confidence. L1 = LaFrance, carrying the Cold War / COG reading. L2 = the 2016 Loudoun County land-use proceeding (CMPT-2016-0001), carrying the physical and quantitative material. The Times-Mirror, Loudoun Now, four advocacy organisations and Data Center Dynamics all read ONE county file and are therefore not independent of each other — but they are all independent of L1, because the file exists whether or not LaFrance ever wrote a word.
lineage.collapse_or_note: Six named reporting and advocacy bodies = one public file. That is still a real second origin, because the file has an existence independent of the Cold War literature.

candidates.verification_state: V0-UNRESOLVED — every source behind this record is SEARCH-SNIPPET-ONLY, FETCH-BLOCKED or CITED-BY-OTHERS-NOT-SEEN. No citation in this file has been resolved to bytes by any agent.
candidates.mundane_alternative: A07 — an AT&T long-haul microwave and switching station, hardened in the 1960s to DoD's AUTOVON survivability specification, which since divestiture has become an ordinary piece of AT&T network real estate and which in 2016 the company wanted to expand into a conventional carrier data centre, on a mountaintop it already owned, in the county that hosts more data-centre capacity than anywhere on earth. WHAT WOULD DISTINGUISH IT: the 2016 file itself — a data-centre build has a named electrical service agreement with Dominion, a cooling design, a raised-floor or rack layout and a stated IT load, all of which appear in commission-permit engineering exhibits; a hardened federal build has none of those and instead has shielding, filtration and berthing. Second discriminator: the Loudoun parcel and deed chain — a federal leasehold, easement or restrictive covenant on an AT&T fee parcel is unusual and would be visible. Third: whether the 1960s structure carries any NTIA federal frequency assignment as distinct from AT&T's FCC licences.
candidates.claim_origin: The site's identification as a Cold War hardened installation traces to Albert LaFrance's coldwar-c4i.net [VA-1] page (see the chain entry). The 2016 material has an entirely separate and much better origin: a live Loudoun County land-use proceeding, reported contemporaneously and independently by the Loudoun Times-Mirror and Loudoun Now, with advocacy documentation from the Piedmont Environmental Council, Friends of the Blue Ridge Mountains and the Loudoun County Preservation and Conservation Coalition, and trade coverage by Data Center Dynamics. The 'Project Aurelia' internal name and the confidentiality clause appear to originate with the Times-Mirror's own reporting on the application file. The Higgins quotation originates with the Times-Mirror. I could not date the Times-Mirror article precisely from the index.
candidates.expected_records: LOUDOUN COUNTY LAND DEVELOPMENT FILE for CMPT-2016-0001 and CMPT-2020-0005 — X3, and reachable: Loudoun publishes its land-development records. This is the highest-value single acquisition on this beat. LOUDOUN COUNTY PARCEL / DEED — X3, universal floor. LOUDOUN BUILDING PERMITS for the original 1960s construction — X0 to X1; county digitisation rarely reaches 1963 and federal-adjacent construction on private fee land may or may not have been permitted locally. USGS HTMC — X3; the ridge is well-mapped and a 1960s structure should appear across editions. FCC ASR/ULS — X3 for the towers. NTIA GMF — X0, withheld by aggregation. MILCON / FPDS / FRPP / GSA — X0, AT&T is not an appropriated entity and the parcel is private fee. NEPA — X0 for the 1960s build; X1 for the 2016 proposal only if a federal nexus existed, which nothing suggests. CREST/DTIC — X0, facility partly operational.
candidates.confidence_note: EXIST here is close to certain and cheaply provable. The 2016 expansion is documented to a standard rare anywhere in this register. The COG function is a single inference wearing local-news clothing. I want to flag a specific hazard: the 2016 controversy generated a great deal of text that reads like evidence about the 1960s facility and is not — residents' and reporters' speculation about what is under the mountain is downstream of LaFrance and of each other, and a naive ingest will read it as dozens of converging sources. It is one source and a county file.

propositions.statement: A substantial subsurface structure exists on the ridge of Short Hill Mountain.
propositions.assessment: This is the strongest EXIST on the beat, for an unusual reason: in 2016 AT&T itself filed a land-use application with Loudoun County to build a 160,000 sq ft aboveground structure adjoining, in the reporting's words, 'its already-existing underground facility'. A corporation's own filing with a zoning authority, describing its own property, is a party with authority over the fact under §3.4(e), and the county is the record custodian. If CMPT-2016-0001 resolves and contains that description, this is a D4 row and EXIST reaches A on a single document. Conditional: A on the county file; B without it, on CLUI plus multiple bylined local-press accounts.
supporting: Loudoun County commission permit proceeding, reported application CMPT-2016-0001, 2016 — AT&T application to build adjacent to an existing underground facility
CLUI Land Use Database, AT&T Short Hill Mountain Site — underground bunker of at least several thousand square feet with a drive-in entrance
Loudoun Times-Mirror reporting, 'What's up there? There's more than meets the eye to Short Hill Mountain'
Loudoun Now reporting, June 2016, on the application's withdrawal
propositions.proposed_band: X
propositions.diagnosticity_note: The mundane null for Loudoun County — a data centre, in the county that is Data Center Alley — predicts an underground building poorly. Data centres in Loudoun are built at grade in commodity industrial shells. A 1960s earth-covered mountaintop structure is not what A07 produces. So EXIST is discriminating here in a way it usually is not.

propositions.statement: The subsurface structure is engineered against nuclear blast beyond ordinary construction for a telecommunications building.
propositions.assessment: Asserted by coldwar-c4i.net in the same terms as the rest of the chain — earth-covered, drive-through decontamination bay, blast-resistant microwave antennas, physical security beyond conventional AT&T practice. No instance-level engineering document seen. Conditional: this is where the beat's discipline bites hardest. Even a resolved county building-permit file is D2 at best for HARDEN unless it recites blast valves, shielding or a design standard on its face, exactly as the calibration set holds for Fairview: the licensing or permitting authority has authority over the permit, not over the hardening.
supporting: coldwar-c4i.net [VA-1] page — earth-covered underground building, drive-through entrance-decontamination area, blast-resistant terrestrial microwave antennas
undercutting: No design standard, as-built, or specification naming this site was found. For a privately financed carrier building this is an X0/X1 silence and carries little weight, but it does mean the claim is one compiler deep.
propositions.proposed_band: X
propositions.diagnosticity_note: A drive-through decontamination bay is the one reported feature that no mundane alternative for a mountaintop microwave station produces. Earth cover, generators, fuel and security are all D0. If the decontamination bay can be evidenced from a filed drawing or a georeferenced photograph by a resolvable observer, HARDEN moves; without it, HARDEN is a restatement of the chain-level claim.

propositions.statement: The site is owned and operated by AT&T, and has hosted a federal government activity since approximately 1963.
propositions.assessment: AT&T ownership is not in dispute and is trivially checkable in the Loudoun parcel record. The federal-activity half rests on one on-the-record statement: Supervisor Geary Higgins (R-Catoctin), quoted in the Loudoun Times-Mirror, saying 'This is and has been a government site up there since 1963.' Under §5.4 he passes the identity gate comfortably — an elected county supervisor is resolvable in records created for entirely unrelated purposes and predating the claim — and attestation custody is satisfied by a bylined quotation in named local press. He fails the position-to-know clause: nothing places a county supervisor in a role that would give him authority over what a classified tenant does on a mountaintop. His statement is therefore a resolvable named person's belief, not a knowledgeable account, and it enters at low diagnosticity. Conditional: CONTROL(AT&T) reaches A on the parcel record; CONTROL(federal activity) is capped at E by CAP-2b on the current record.
supporting: Loudoun Times-Mirror — Supervisor Geary Higgins quoted on a government presence since 1963
Loudoun Times-Mirror — AT&T invoked a confidentiality clause regarding the 2016 project, internally 'Project Aurelia'
Reporting that visitors to the site require a background check
undercutting: A background-check requirement for site access is standard for critical carrier infrastructure and for any facility carrying government traffic under contract; it does not require a federal tenant.
A confidentiality clause in a commercial land-use filing is ordinary corporate practice for network plant and is equally consistent with a competitively sensitive data-centre build.
propositions.proposed_band: X
propositions.diagnosticity_note: Higgins's statement is the only claim-property item here — it is about the claim (a government site), not about the place. Everything else (security, confidentiality, background checks) is place-property and D0 against A07. That asymmetry is precisely what CAP-2b measures, and it is why a site this visibly interesting still cannot carry a CONTROL(federal) grade.

propositions.statement: The 2016 'Project Aurelia' proposal specified a 160,000 sq ft, 35 ft tall aboveground structure with eight 4 MW standby generators, a large cooling plant, roughly 2 million gallons of water annually, and about 60 staff on a 24/7 basis.
propositions.assessment: This is the single most quantitatively specific thing on the whole beat and it comes from a public county land-use file, which is the best custody available to me. The numbers are internally coherent and, read together, they are a data-centre profile: roughly 32 MW of standby generation against 160,000 sq ft and 60 staff is on the order of 200 W/sq ft, which is IT load, not office load. Conditional: if the county file resolves, this is D4 for FEATURE and D3 as an UNDERCUTS row against the COG reading of the 2016 expansion, because the null predicts it far better than the proposition does.
supporting: Loudoun County commission permit file as reported by Loudoun Times-Mirror, Loudoun Now, Piedmont Environmental Council, Friends of the Blue Ridge Mountains, and Data Center Dynamics
Data Center Dynamics — trade-press framing of the proposal as a data-centre build 'in disguise... despite repeated claims to the contrary'
propositions.proposed_band: X
propositions.diagnosticity_note: This row cuts AGAINST the interesting hypothesis and that is why it belongs here. A 32 MW standby plant and a 2-million-gallon annual water draw are what a hyperscale or carrier data centre needs; they are not what a hardened relocation facility needs, and they are radically disproportionate to a 1960s tropo station's load. The register should record that the most specific, best-custodied document on this site points at the mundane explanation for the 2016 works. It says nothing either way about the 1960s structure underneath.

propositions.statement: The underground facility serves or served a federal continuity-of-government or national-security function beyond commercial carriage.
propositions.assessment: Inherits the chain-level problem entirely: one compiler's hedged inference plus one county supervisor's belief. Nothing instance-specific and claim-bearing was found. Conditional: E at best under CAP-2b even with receipts, until a claim-property instance record appears.
supporting: coldwar-c4i.net [VA-1] — inference of a classified COG programme
Higgins quotation
undercutting: The 2016 expansion profile is a commercial-infrastructure profile (see FEAT above).

AT&T's stated position through the proceeding was that the project was not a data centre and it declined to say what it was — which is uninformative in both directions and should not be read as confirmation.
propositions.proposed_band: X
propositions.diagnosticity_note: Secrecy is not diagnostic. A corporation declining to describe a facility discriminates between 'classified federal tenant' and 'competitively sensitive commercial build' not at all — both predict it strongly. This is the specific inferential error the local coverage and every downstream retelling made, and the register should say so.

lineage.assessment: TWO. L1 = Jon Elliston, 'Big Hole, Deep Secret', Indy Week, 13 December 2000 — a real, datable, bylined origin, from which every circulating instance of $27,000 / $7 million / Muirhead Construction / four years / 100,000 sq ft / '45 years' descends. candidates.verification_state: V0-UNRESOLVED — every source behind this record is SEARCH-SNIPPET-ONLY, FETCH-BLOCKED or CITED-BY-OTHERS-NOT-SEEN. No citation in this file has been resolved to bytes by any agent.
candidates.mundane_alternative: A07 — a hardened AT&T AUTOVON switching terminal and troposcatter station, built with AT&T capital on land AT&T bought, serving DoD voice traffic under contract, whose secrecy is contractual rather than constitutional and which was decommissioned when troposcatter and AUTOVON became obsolete. This accounts for the scale, the secrecy, the security, the 45-year operating life and the 2008 shutdown. WHAT WOULD DISTINGUISH IT: berthing and life support sized for a population rather than a crew; a federal leasehold or covenant in the Chatham County deed chain; and — the cheapest test available — whether the Greenbrier switchboard appearance is a trunk group to a switch (mundane) or a dedicated station line to a habitable facility (not mundane). The second is answerable from the Greenbrier's own publicly displayed equipment.
candidates.claim_origin: Jon Elliston, 'Big Hole, Deep Secret', Indy Week, 13 December 2000. This is a real, datable, bylined origin for the site's factual record and I regard it as the most important single citation on this beat. Everything downstream that quotes $27,000, $7 million, Muirhead Construction, four years, 100,000 square feet or '45 years' is repeating Elliston, including War History Online, OnlyInYourState, thetownofliberty.com, Free Republic threads, realtor blog posts and, in part, Wikipedia. Elliston later wrote for Indy Week on national-security topics generally, which makes him a resolvable named journalist rather than an anonymous poster. The COG-programme framing is separately LaFrance's. Kastleman 2020 is a scholarly treatment that engages the site as memory and landscape and appears to draw on family and community testimony as well as on the existing record; it is not an independent documentary origin. I found no appearance of the Chatham material earlier than 2000 in the index, but I did NOT run the canonical ORIGIN corpora — no Wayback CDX, no IA full-text, no Chronicling America sweep of Chatham County and Durham papers from 1960–1968, which is where a construction-era local story would live. Absent that negative receipt no ORIGIN proposition can be offered, and I decline to offer one.
candidates.expected_records: CHATHAM COUNTY DEED AND ASSESSOR — X3, the universal floor, and unusually promising here because Elliston's figures suggest he read them. The 1960s AT&T acquisition should be in the deed books. NORTH CAROLINA / DURHAM TRADE AND BUSINESS RECORDS for Muirhead Construction Company — X1, a named general contractor on a four-year $7M job in the 1960s should leave a trade-press or corporate trace independent of every source above. LOCAL PRESS 1960–1968 (Chatham County, Durham, Chapel Hill) — X1 and flagged ARCHIVE-GAP: Chronicling America's free corpus is copyright-bounded after 1963, so the most likely construction-era coverage sits in exactly the window the free corpus does not reach. This is a real and specific archive gap, not a mystery. USGS HTMC — X3. FCC ASR dismantle record for the tropo reflectors — X3 and directly checkable. MILCON / FPDS / FRPP / GSA — X0 throughout, AT&T is not an appropriated entity. CREST / DTIC — X0 for a facility of this vintage whose programme may still be classified, and X2 only if the programme has been declassified, which nothing indicates.
candidates.confidence_note: This is the best-documented Project Office and the one where a determined researcher with unblocked access could most quickly produce a genuinely A-grade EXIST and a defensible B on the AUTOVON function. The COG-sheltering claim is a different animal and I want to be blunt: it is one inference plus a switchboard label, and the switchboard label — the only good evidence — supports a communications relationship and not a sheltering role. Those two propositions get conflated in every popular account and the register should hold them apart.

propositions.statement: A large multi-level subsurface structure exists at the site.
propositions.assessment: Supported by an unusually good combination for this beat: a bylined investigative newspaper article that appears to have worked from county records and named local interviews, a peer-reviewed scholarly article, a CLUI site entry with independent photography, and a large public photographic set. Conditional: the Chatham County deed and assessor records plus the reported construction figures would very likely carry EXIST to A or B once pulled. Elliston's reported $27,000 land purchase and $7 million construction cost read like deed-book and contract figures, which is a reason to expect the underlying records to exist.
supporting: Elliston, 'Big Hole, Deep Secret', Indy Week, 13 Dec 2000 — $27,000 land purchase, four-year $7 million excavation and construction, Durham's Muirhead Construction Company, multi-floor 100,000 sq ft bunker
CLUI Land Use Database, AT&T Chatham Big Hole Site — underground bunker of at least several thousand square feet with a drive-in entrance
Kastleman, 'Big Hole: Excavating intimate histories of a nuclear homefront', Critical Military Studies 7(4), 2020

propositions.proposed_band: X
propositions.diagnosticity_note: A 100,000 sq ft multi-floor excavation is not on the universal-D0 list in the way a generic 'hole' is — the volume itself is an expected-record generator (spoil signature, hauling contracts, a named general contractor). Muirhead Construction Company of Durham is a nameable, checkable corporate entity, and a contractor's own records or a trade-press mention would be independent of every source above.

propositions.statement: The subsurface structure is approximately 100,000 square feet across multiple floors, buried roughly 30 feet, with walls several feet thick.
propositions.assessment: The 100,000 sq ft and multi-floor figures come from Elliston 2000. The '30 feet underground', 'walls several feet thick covered in copper', 'shock-absorbing springs' and 'plumbing made out of rubber' details are, per Wikipedia's own framing, descriptions BY AREA RESIDENTS AND PERSONS EMPLOYED IN CONSTRUCTION — that is, unresolved third-party attestation, not measurement. The copper cladding and rubber plumbing are plausible as lay descriptions of RF shielding and of flexible service penetrations at a shock-isolated structure, which is a point in their favour, but plausibility is not evidence. Conditional: EXTENT sits at D unless a drawing, permit or assessor record resolves — which is exactly the KUMMSC pattern in the calibration set, where existence is solid and extent is inferred.
supporting: Elliston, Indy Week, 2000
Resident and construction-worker descriptions as relayed by Wikipedia and downstream sources
undercutting: CLUI, which visited, says only 'at least several thousand square feet' — an order of magnitude below the 100,000 sq ft figure. Two compilations disagree by 20x and neither shows its working.
propositions.proposed_band: X
propositions.diagnosticity_note: The CLUI / Elliston discrepancy is the most useful thing in this row. It is a live, checkable disagreement between two of the better sources on the beat, and resolving it against a county assessor record or a drawing would do more for this entry than any amount of further reading.

propositions.statement: The facility served as an AUTOVON switching centre and as part of a continuity-of-government communications system.
propositions.assessment: The AUTOVON half is consistently reported and is consistent with the documented network. The COG half rests, again, on LaFrance's inference — with one genuinely independent and genuinely diagnostic item: the Greenbrier bunker's switchboard is reported to bear the legends 'CHATAM' and 'HGRSTOWN'. The Greenbrier is a declassified, publicly toured federal COG facility; its equipment labels are third-party observable by anyone who buys a ticket, and they were created by the federal operator for its own purposes, not to advance anyone's claim. Conditional: a receipted, georeferenced photograph of that panel by a resolvable named observer would be a D2–D3 CLAIM-PROPERTY row and would move FUNCTION(COG) off the floor for the first time on this beat.
supporting: Greenbrier bunker switchboard reportedly labelled 'CHATAM' and 'HGRSTOWN' (coldwarcomms.org, CLUI)
coldwar-c4i.net and Wikipedia on AUTOVON role and the 1966 in-service date
Elliston, Indy Week, 2000 — 45 years of AT&T operation, AUTOVON
undercutting: A COG facility having a labelled trunk to a hardened carrier switch proves a communications relationship, not a sheltering role. The label is evidence for FUNCTION(COG communications node); it is not evidence for FUNCTION(relocation site for officials), and those must be graded separately.
propositions.proposed_band: X
propositions.diagnosticity_note: Highest-diagnosticity single item found anywhere on this beat, and it is worth stating why. Under the mundane null — a pure DoD AUTOVON switch with no COG relationship — a congressional relocation bunker's switchboard would not carry a dedicated labelled appearance for this specific station. Under the proposition it is close to required. That is an E3/A1 or better cell. It is also currently unreceipted, which is the whole problem.

propositions.statement: As of the 2010s the facility is non-operational or mothballed, with tropospheric scatter antennas removed, and remains in AT&T ownership.
propositions.assessment: Reported by a 2008 personal blog post ('Secret Chatham AT&T bunker closes'), by CLUI, and by later summaries which say equipment was removed in summer 2008, the site briefly appeared abandoned, then reopened without the tropo antennas. Reports conflict on whether it is presently in use. (2) The current-facility description originates with Vital Records Inc.'s own website. The 1968 announcement is referenced within CLUI's account and is very likely traceable to a contemporaneous New Jersey newspaper item, which would be an independent 1968-dated origin — that is a concrete, findable target and I did not pursue it.
candidates.expected_records: MORRIS COUNTY NJ DEED for the 1995 AT&T-to-VRI transfer — X3 and inside the digitisation window; the single best acquisition here. MUNICIPAL ASSESSMENT RECORD — X3, and would resolve the square-footage conflict directly. NEW JERSEY LOCAL PRESS 1968–1970 — X1 flagged ARCHIVE-GAP; the free Chronicling America corpus is copyright-bounded well before 1968, so this needs a paid or library newspaper database. candidates.confidence_note: High confidence in existence and in the conversion story; the register's product here is the documented pathway and the square-footage conflict, not a secret. I would rate this among the most likely candidates on the beat to end up entirely mundane and entirely true, which is the correct outcome for many entries and should not be treated as a failed lead.

propositions.statement: A two-level subsurface structure exists at the site.

Conditional: A is realistic once the Morris County deed recording the 1995 AT&T-to-VRI sale and the borough or township assessment record resolve. Both should exist and both should be findable — a 1995 commercial transfer is inside the digitisation window for most New Jersey jurisdictions.

propositions.statement: The structure is two levels, at approximately 30 and 50 feet below grade, of between 86,000 and 125,000 square feet.
propositions.assessment: There is a live and specific quantitative conflict here that nobody appears to have noticed. CLUI says 86,000 square feet. The operator says more than 125,000 square feet of usable space across two floors at 30 and 50 feet. A 45 per cent discrepancy between an independent surveyor and the owner is not noise. The likeliest reconciliation is that the figures measure different things (gross structure versus usable including mezzanine or added build-out since 1995) but that is my inference, not a finding. Conditional: D until an assessment record, a filed floor plan or a fire-code occupancy filing resolves it — the KUMMSC pattern again.
supporting: CLUI — 86,000 sq ft, two levels, concrete walls more than 2 feet thick, entirely cased in steel
Vital Records Inc. — two underground floors at 30 and 50 feet below ground, more than 125,000 sq ft usable
undercutting: The two figures contradict each other and one of them is self-published by a party selling space by the square foot, which is a commercial incentive to state the larger number.
propositions.proposed_band: X
propositions.diagnosticity_note: Not about hardening at all — about whether the register can carry a number. The operator's figure is SELF-PUBLISHED and under §2.4 is excluded from V outright, which means on the current record the only admissible figure is CLUI's, and CLUI's is unsourced. That is the honest position and it is more useful than splitting the difference.

propositions.statement: The structure was built as a nuclear-hardened facility, with concrete walls over two feet thick, a full steel casing, and three weeks of on-site life support and generation for a staff of thirty.
propositions.assessment: The steel casing is the notable claim — a full metallic envelope is a shielding measure, not a structural one, and it is a genuine hardening signature rather than a generic one. It is asserted by CLUI, and the life-support and staffing figures likewise. The operator's own material asserts the hardened origin as a selling point, which under §2.4 makes it SELF-PUBLISHED and inadmissible. Conditional: C to B if AT&T corporate engineering literature or a 1968-era permit or trade-press account resolves; D otherwise.
supporting: CLUI — walls of concrete more than 2 feet thick, entirely cased in steel, designed to withstand nuclear attack and operate 24 hours for up to three weeks
CLUI — accommodations and supplies for the 30 people who operated the centre
undercutting: Operator marketing describing the facility as nuclear-hardened is SELF-PUBLISHED and excluded from V; it cannot corroborate CLUI even though it agrees with it. Agreement between an independent surveyor and the owner's sales copy is not two lineages, especially where the surveyor may have taken the description from the owner.
propositions.proposed_band: X
propositions.diagnosticity_note: A complete steel envelope is E3/A0-ish against A07 — an ordinary telephone exchange or commercial records warehouse is not cased in steel, because the only reason to do it is electromagnetic shielding. If that single feature can be receipted from a drawing, a permit or a resolvable direct observation, it does more work than the entire rest of this entry.

propositions.statement: The building served as AT&T's principal network operations centre for more than a decade, and now serves as a commercial records-storage, tape-vaulting and data-centre facility.
propositions.assessment: The historic NOC role is asserted by CLUI and is the kind of fact that AT&T's own corporate history, trade press of the period, and 1968–1970 New Jersey newspapers would document. The current commercial function is uncontested and is affirmatively documented by the operator's ordinary business existence. Conditional: the present-day function reaches A trivially on a business filing plus a lease; the historic NOC role is a good B target.

Vital Records Inc. facility listing — tape vaulting and data centre

candidates.mundane_alternative: A07 — a Bell System L-4 coaxial main station, one of over a hundred, hardened to the network-wide standard of its route class because AT&T hardened the whole L-4 build, carrying ordinary commercial long-distance traffic alongside government traffic, decommissioned when the technology died and now a distressed commercial property. WHAT WOULD DISTINGUISH IT from something more: nothing found so far suggests anything more, and the register should say that. candidates.expected_records: BURT COUNTY NE DEED AND ASSESSOR — X3, universal floor, and here doubly promising because a live listing implies a recent, recorded, digitised chain of title. FCC ASR for the 329 ft tower — X3, and the single cheapest identifier-bearing verification available on this beat. FCC ULS microwave path licences — X3 for the historical route. USGS HTMC — X3; a 1966 build should appear across editions and the temporal stack would date it. BELL SYSTEM PRACTICES / AT&T ROUTE AND PLANT LITERATURE — X2 and the decisive record for HARDEN. NEBRASKA DEQ / EPCRA TIER II for the fuel and battery inventory — X1, obtainable by state request, and directly diagnostic of autonomy. MILCON/FRPP/GSA/FPDS — X0, private carrier plant. What I want to flag is that this is the template case for the entire Long Lines corpus: several hundred similar sites exist, they are all described in similar language by one compilation, and the register must not ingest three hundred entries whose HARDEN grade all descends from one terminus. Getting the underlying Bell System document once fixes the whole class; getting it never means the whole class sits at C forever, correctly.

propositions.assessment: Unusually well positioned for verification: the property is on the open commercial market with a listed address, a listed price and a listed square footage, which means a brokerage listing, a county parcel record, an FCC ASR registration for the tower and a marketing fly-through video all point at the same object. Conditional: A is realistic via A1-alt plus the Burt County parcel record. Note the tower is the easiest single verification on this beat — a 329-foot registered structure has an ASR number and published coordinates.

The Vigilant Prairie Project — Lyons page
propositions.proposed_band: X
propositions.diagnosticity_note: The tower is the diagnostic anchor, not the hole: a 329-foot self-supporting lattice tower carrying horn-reflector antennas is an unambiguous Long Lines signature and is registered with the FCC. It ties the parcel to the network with an identifier.

propositions.statement: The building has blast doors closed by an automatic seal-up system, a decontamination shower, gas-turbine emergency power, and a positive-pressure filtered ventilation system to exclude fallout.
propositions.assessment: This is the most specific hardening description I found for any Long Lines site, and it reads like a transcription of a Bell System engineering description rather than like enthusiast prose — 'seal-up system' is a term of art. Its visible source is long-lines.net, which per the source registry is P4/T4 and is a compilation that names its primaries. Under §5.1.3, if the underlying Bell System Practice or route/plant document resolves, THAT is the lineage and the compiler scores nothing; if it does not resolve, long-lines.net is one T4 terminus at D2 and CAP-1 binds. This is precisely the branch the calibration set requires be computed and published for Fairview, and the same branch applies here. Conditional: B if the primary resolves, C if it does not.
supporting: long-lines.net Lyons NE — blast doors with automatic seal-up, decontamination shower, gas-turbine engine-alternator, positive-pressure filtered ventilation
undercutting: The current brokerage listing states the building is decommissioned and that not all building systems are functional — which undercuts any present-tense hardening claim while leaving the historical one intact.
propositions.proposed_band: X
propositions.diagnosticity_note: Blast doors with an automatic seal-up system and CBR-filtered positive-pressure ventilation are not producible by any mundane alternative for a telephone building. This is a genuine E3/A0 feature set. The entire question is custody: is this a real Bell System description or a compiler's reconstruction? That is answerable and unanswered.

propositions.statement: The station was an L-4 transcontinental coaxial main station whose significance derived in part from its proximity to Strategic Air Command headquarters at Offutt AFB.
propositions.assessment: The L-4 main-station role is straightforward network history and is supported by the Long Lines corpus and by the FAS L-4 Transcontinental Cable System page. The Offutt-proximity significance claim is softer — proximity is not a function, and under §2.4 an adjacent installation's importance is not support for a proposition about this parcel. Conditional: FUNCTION(L-4 main station) is a good B or A target on route documentation; FUNCTION(SAC-supporting) should be graded separately and is currently unsupported.
supporting: long-lines.net — Lyons as an L-4 transcontinental main station
FAS, L-4 Transcontinental Cable System page
Fairview KS material describing the same route's connection to Offutt
undercutting: 'Close to Offutt therefore nationally important' is the ADJACENT trap. It is the same inferential move the calibration set rejects for Project Gasbuggy and Dulce and it should be rejected here.
propositions.proposed_band: X
propositions.diagnosticity_note: Proximity is not support. I am flagging this explicitly because the Long Lines literature makes this move constantly — every site near a base is described as therefore strategic — and an uncritical ingest will convert geography into function across hundreds of sites.

candidates.era: Built by AT&T Long Lines in the 1960s; acquired and rebuilt as a commercial data centre from 2004; clients from 2006; still operating.

location.description: In farmland north of Des Moines, in the Boone, Iowa area, with a microwave relay tower on the surface.
location.basis: County and general placement from the CLUI entry and the operator's material. The operator gives a Des Moines business address (3101 Ingersoll Ave) which is an office, not the facility. No facility coordinate resolved and none asserted.

lineage.assessment: TWO, but they carry different things. (1) Site history: CLUI plus the Long Lines corpus, both attributing construction and ownership to AT&T Long Lines. (2) Hardening figures: the qsl.net transcription, routed through Hackaday (2017) and the operator's marketing. Perhaps thirty pages state the 20-megaton figure for this building; they are ONE lineage.
lineage.collapse_or_note: A TRANSPOSITION plus a SCOPE ERROR in one candidate. The operator asserts the building was 'purpose-built by the military' as a 'former Government Command Bunker'; every account independent of the operator attributes it to AT&T. And a programme-level hardness class is applied to an instance whose class is undocumented — while the same corpus states many L-3I facilities were designed for about 2 psi, two orders of magnitude away from the '50 PSI extremely hard' class being borrowed.

candidates.verification_state: V0-UNRESOLVED — every source behind this record is SEARCH-SNIPPET-ONLY, FETCH-BLOCKED or CITED-BY-OTHERS-NOT-SEEN. No citation in this file has been resolved to bytes by any agent.
candidates.mundane_alternative: A07 — an AT&T Long Lines equipment building, hardened to whatever the route standard was, sold off when the microwave network was retired, rebuilt with a multi-million-dollar investment as an ordinary commercial colocation facility whose marketing leans on its Cold War provenance because that is a selling point in the disaster-recovery market. WHAT WOULD DISTINGUISH IT: the Boone County deed chain (was any grantor a federal entity?), an FCC ASR and ULS history for the tower (was the licensee ever anyone but AT&T?), and any instance-level engineering document. All three are checkable and all three point the same way on present evidence.
candidates.claim_origin: Two origins, and the interesting one is a transposition. (1) The site's real history originates with the AT&T Long Lines record and is carried by CLUI and the Long Lines compilation corpus. (2) The hardening figures originate, as far as I can trace them, with a document transcribed at qsl.net/n9zia/Nuclear_Design.htm under the title 'Nuclear Design of AT&T Equipment', which sets out AT&T design assumptions — 2.5 miles from a 20-megaton blast, 1000 mph wind, 40 G shock, and an 'Extremely Hard Design (50 PSI)' class. That programme-level document is the source of the figure that now appears, applied to individual buildings, in the Hackaday Long Lines feature (2017), in InfoBunker's marketing, in Data Center Knowledge's coverage, and in dozens of directory and listicle pages. I could not establish what the qsl.net page is a transcription OF — whether a Bell System Practice, a Bell Laboratories Record article, an AT&T presentation, or something else — and that is the single most consequential untraced item on this beat, because it is the origin of the most-copied number in the entire Long Lines literature.
candidates.expected_records: BOONE COUNTY IA DEED AND ASSESSOR — X3, universal floor, and decisive for CONTROL. FCC ASR AND ULS for the tower, including licence history — X3, and would show every licensee since registration. IOWA DNR FACILITY RECORD — X2, already indexed and machine-accessible, and would carry tank and generator detail directly relevant to autonomy claims. IOWA EPCRA TIER II — X1 by state request; fuel and battery inventory is one of the sharpest hardening signatures available and is not published. THE UNDERLYING AT&T DESIGN DOCUMENT behind the qsl.net transcription — X2 and the highest-leverage single acquisition for the whole Long Lines class. MILCON/DD-1391 — X0 if AT&T-financed, which the evidence indicates; X3 only if the 'purpose-built by the military' claim were true, which means that claim generates a testable, high-expectation negative. CREST/DTIC — X0.
candidates.confidence_note: The most instructive candidate on the beat, and the one I would most want the register to publish, because publishing it correctly means grading an A-or-B existence beside an unsupportable hardening claim on the same page. Note the useful asymmetry the ERP table produces: the operator's claim that the military built the facility PREDICTS records that should exist (a MILCON line, a federal deed, a service real-property entry) and none has been found, while the AT&T account predicts records that plausibly do exist and were not searched. That is a case where silence is genuinely informative, and it is informative against the dramatic claim.

propositions.statement: The structure is three-foot reinforced concrete, more than 50 feet underground, and was designed to survive a 20-megaton nuclear detonation at 2.5 miles.
propositions.assessment: This is the beat's cleanest §2.5 case and I want to set it out carefully. Every quantitative hardening figure in circulation for this building comes from the operator's own marketing, reproduced verbatim by data-centre directories, listicles and trade blogs. The operator is the party advancing the claim and the claim is the product; the material is SELF-PUBLISHED and, for the hardening proposition specifically, self-attesting. Under §2.4 it is excluded from V entirely. Worse, the '20 megaton at 2.5 miles' figure is not a measurement of this building at all: it is a NETWORK-WIDE AT&T design assumption for one hardness class, documented at the programme level, transposed onto an individual instance. That is the CLASS-to-INSTANCE error §2.4 exists to block. Conditional: with the operator's material excluded, V for HARDEN is empty and this proposition would sit at F, not D — it is not that the evidence is weak, it is that there is no admissible evidence at all.
undercutting: The '20 megaton at 2.5 miles / 1000 mph wind / 40 G' figures are a programme-level AT&T design criterion, not an instance specification, and applying them here is unsupported.

The operator's description of the site as 'a former Government Command Bunker... purpose-built by the military' is contradicted by every independent account, all of which attribute construction to AT&T Long Lines.

Operators of converted bunkers have a direct commercial incentive to state the strongest available hardening claim, which makes their assertions anti-diagnostic: the more dramatic the number, the more it is explained by the sales motive.
