comms.mundane_explanation: Large carrier capital projects at existing network nodes are routine, and $61 million, while extraordinary for a relay hut, is unremarkable for a core network node or a substantial data-hall build. Even a confirmed figure would be consistent with the commercial null.

comms.claim: Grokipedia pages on 'Project Offices' and on the Hadley PACCS facility constitute additional sources.
comms.origin: Grokipedia, a machine-generated encyclopedia, mirroring the corresponding Wikipedia articles.
comms.why_hollow: Under §3.3 these are POST-2022-UNATTRIBUTED and sit on the versioned blocklist of machine-generated corpora: T5, zero contribution to every condition, zero lineages, retained and displayed. I record them because they surfaced repeatedly in this session's search results ALONGSIDE the Wikipedia articles they mirror, which creates exactly the false appearance of breadth the rule exists to prevent. An automated ingest counting distinct domains would score this as two sources. It is one, and the one is already T4.
comms.mundane_explanation: A machine-generated encyclopedia restated an existing encyclopedia article. Nothing was learned and nothing was added.

comms.claim: Netcong, New Jersey was one of the AT&T Project Offices.
comms.origin: A conflation in this session's own search results, where a query naming several candidate sites returned the Netcong CLUI entry among Project Office material and the summary presented them as members of one set.
comms.why_hollow: Recorded as a finding against my own process rather than against a source. The Project Office chain, per both coldwar-c4i.net and CLUI, is five mid-Atlantic TROPOSCATTER stations running Hagerstown–Short Hill–Peters Mountain–Buckingham–Chatham. Netcong is a different object: AT&T's underground network operations centre in northern New Jersey, with no troposcatter role reported. I have excluded it from the chain entry and given it its own. The near-miss is worth publishing because a candidate-set rule (§9.2 C1c) is only as good as the set's boundary, and an erroneously admitted sixth member would have inflated M and diluted every genuine member's grade.
comms.mundane_explanation: Two AT&T underground buildings of the same era in adjacent regions, described in similar language by the same compilations, retrieved by one query.

folklore.claim: 'Thomas Castello', an alleged RAND-employed Dulce security technician who escaped with the 'Dulce Papers', thirty photographs and a videotape
folklore.origin: The persona circulates c. 1987-1991 within the Dulce cluster; Thomas Allen LeVesque, writing as 'Jason Bishop III', is reported to have admitted to author Adam Gorightly before his death in December 2018 that Castello never existed and that the material was creative writing. Christa Tilton is separately reported to have reached the same conclusion.
folklore.why_hollow: The person does not resolve outside the claim. Under BES 5.4 a name that resolves to nothing in any record created for an unrelated purpose scores D0 regardless of how much text is attributed to it, and the attestation-custody rule means an anonymous account of what a named person said is one lineage with whoever is asserting - never with the person. Two caveats I insist on: the admission reaches me second-hand, after the admitter's death, through named but non-institutional channels, so the R1 route is weaker than the register's calibration presents it; and I did not run the negative search that would independently establish non-existence.
folklore.mundane_explanation: A pseudonymous authorial persona created as fiction inside a milieu already saturated by a documented AFOSI disinformation operation against Paul Bennewitz.

folklore.claim: The 'New World Airport Commission' named on the Denver International Airport dedication capstone is a New World Order body
folklore.origin: Absorbed into the DIA folklore from the mid-1990s, principally via Alex Christopher's 'Pandora's Box' (1993) and 'Pandora's Box II' (1996).
folklore.why_hollow: The Denver Public Library holds a processed archival collection, 'New World Airport Commission Records', described as a public-relations body for the airport's opening, active 1994, 1997 and 1998, with correspondence to and from its president Charles Ansbacher. A finding aid at the holding repository is a T1 record from a body with authority over the fact of what it holds, and it describes a temporary municipal PR commission. This is an affirmative undercutting row, not an absence. FETCH BLOCKED - I have the finding aid's summary, not the finding aid.
folklore.mundane_explanation: A temporary civic commission organised to run the opening festivities of a new airport, its name most likely alluding to Dvorak's New World Symphony.

folklore.claim: 'Hangar 18' is a specific structure at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base
folklore.origin: A diffuse mid-century cluster rather than a single text, cemented in the nomenclature by a 1980 feature film of that title - a citogenesis route the register should trace directly.
folklore.why_hollow: The Library of Congress HAER survey records Building 18 in Area B as part of the Power Plant Laboratory Complex, at the northeast corner of C and Fifth Streets - an engine and power-plant research facility, not a hangar. The organisation the claim is actually reaching for, the Foreign Technology Division, occupied Building 856 from the 1970s, becoming FASTC in 1992 and NASIC in 2003. The claim conflates a laboratory building number with a hangar and attaches to it the function of an organisation housed elsewhere. FETCH BLOCKED at loc.gov.
folklore.mundane_explanation: A large, genuinely classified aeronautical research installation whose documented Foreign Technology Division work on recovered SOVIET and CHINESE aircraft is real, misread and misnumbered.

folklore.claim: The specific Denver International Airport figures - eight underground levels, a 4.5 square mile underground city, an 88.5 square mile base
folklore.origin: Phil Schneider, reported by Alex Christopher in 'Pandora's Box II' (1996) as Schneider's own statements.
folklore.why_hollow: The figures have no source and no antecedent, and their route into circulation runs through one man's 1995 lecture circuit. The register should record the consequence: the DIA claim and the '129 DUMBs' claim are ONE lineage, not two, so any treatment of them as mutually reinforcing double-counts a single lecture. Under BES 5.7 this is the non-monotone case where finding a link lowers a grade.
folklore.mundane_explanation: The real subterranean levels beneath the terminal are the inter-concourse passenger train and the abandoned BAE automated baggage system - 26 miles of steel track, retired in 2008 and walled off, which the airport now reportedly intends to open to the public as pedestrian walkways from 2027.

folklore.claim: '1,477 underground bases worldwide' and '129 (or 131) secret underground bases in the United States'
folklore.origin: Phil Schneider's Preparedness Expo lecture, 1995 (sources differ between September and November), deposited on the Internet Archive as 'philexpo'. Schneider died in January 1996, freezing the text as canon.
folklore.why_hollow: No source, no antecedent, no coordinate for any of the 129, no procurement record, no spoil accounting - and thirty years without a list. The figures function as a lineage fingerprint: any page carrying '1,477' or '129 underground bases' is in this lineage regardless of what else it says, and that test survives paraphrase and machine regeneration where shingle-matching does not. NOTE CAREFULLY: this is F, not R. The expected-record negatives here are deep and real and BES 8.4 forbids converting them into refutation - a model that refutes on negatives alone would also have refuted the Greenbrier in 1991.
folklore.mundane_explanation: A number asserted in one lecture and repeated. The genuine referent that makes it superficially plausible is the real and substantial body of documented US hardened underground facilities, which have names, records and coordinates.

folklore.claim: 'Report from Iron Mountain' is a genuine suppressed federal study
folklore.origin: Leonard C. Lewin, Dial Press, 1967, framed as leaked to him by a participant; authorship admitted by Lewin in the New York Times Book Review of 19 March 1972.
folklore.why_hollow: The author confessed in print, under his own name, in a named national periodical, at a fixed date. That is BES 8's R1 branch in its cleanest possible form - an admission by the participant, documentary rather than testimonial - and it stands in instructive contrast to the Dulce R1 route, which rests on a second-hand report of a dead man's admission. The two look identical in a one-line summary and are completely different in kind. Recirculation as authentic continued through 1990s militia bootlegs and persists on live pages in 2026, including machine-generated ones.
folklore.mundane_explanation: A political satire, set at a real underground corporate records-storage facility near Hudson, New York - which is itself a different object again from the Iron Mountain / Boyers, Pennsylvania facility the register already grades at band A. Three distinct things, one word, and BES 11.1 forbids merging them on name similarity.

folklore.claim: A pre-Columbian 'Lizard People' city with a Key Room and gold tablets lies beneath Fort Moore Hill, Los Angeles
folklore.origin: G. Warren Shufelt, on readings from a self-built 'radio X-ray' device; reported by Jean Bosquet, Los Angeles Times, 29 January 1934. The Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors is reported to have approved the excavation contract on 21 February 1933 with Rex McCreary, Warren Shufelt and Ray Martin on a treasure-split basis.
folklore.why_hollow: It was affirmatively tested at the time, by the claimant, with the county's permission, and it failed. A shaft was sunk to roughly 250 feet at the claimed spot; no tunnels and no tablets were found; water and mud entered; funding and press attention ended and the holes were covered. A century of downtown regrading and construction has since constituted an enormous accidental search with an entirely negative result. This is not the argument from silence - it is a failed test, which is affirmative content improbable under the proposition.
folklore.mundane_explanation: A 1930s treasure-hunting venture built on an unvalidated instrument, given administrative cover by a county with nothing to lose and publicity by a metropolitan newspaper with a taste for the story.

folklore.claim: 'Mel's Hole', a bottomless pit on private land nine miles west of Ellensburg, Washington
folklore.origin: A caller identifying himself as Mel Waters on Coast to Coast AM with Art Bell, 21 February 1997, with a follow-up on 24 February 1997 and further appearances in 2000 and 2002.
folklore.why_hollow: Local reporters are described as having searched the Kittitas County records and found no Mel Waters as a property owner, no matching rural parcel, and no employment record for the claimed wife at Central Washington University. County deed and assessor records sit at X3 on the expected-record table - the universal CONUS floor - so this absence is maximally informative rather than routine. A thirty-person ground search of Manastash Ridge in 2002 with GPS and metal detectors, covered by the Seattle Times, found nothing. Jack Powell, then a Washington DNR geologist, stated in 2012 that such a hole is physically impossible and identified a real abandoned gold-mine shaft northwest of Ellensburg, perhaps 300 feet deep, as the plausible substrate. CAVEAT: everything above is journalists reporting that they searched the county record. The record itself is unretrieved, and it is the difference between R and F.
folklore.mundane_explanation: A performed or fabricated call, plausibly built on local knowledge of a real 300-foot abandoned mine shaft on private land.

folklore.claim: A national tunnel network was melted by nuclear subterrene machines, and the absence of spoil proves it
folklore.origin: The inference, not the documents. The documents are genuine 1970s Los Alamos research. The move from 'the AEC patented a rock-melting tunneller' to 'therefore a network was melted' traces to the 1990s fringe-book corpus, principally Richard Sauder's 'Underground Bases and Tunnels' (1995), with Schneider supplying the numbers.
folklore.why_hollow: The 1972 patent's own stated advantage - that the process produces no muck or tailings - is deployed downstream to explain why the most diagnostic possible signal is missing. Spoil-volume signature sits at X3 on the expected-record table, the strongest negative available. A claim structured so that the absence of its own strongest disconfirming signal counts as support has removed its own falsifiability, and under BES 4.4 that collapses to the D0 cell at any volume of assertion. Separately: the programme record indicates transfer in 1975 and quiet termination without a full-scale prototype.
folklore.mundane_explanation: A cancelled civil-tunnelling R&D programme, funded partly by the National Science Foundation, plus the very large body of real, named, documented US deep underground construction - the Rainier Mesa U12 tunnel complex being the clearest instance, with six nuclear weapons-effects tests in U12t alone between 1970 and 1987 and a published DOE historical evaluation.

folklore.claim: 'Western Virginia Office of Controlled Conflict Operations' is an official designation of the Mount Weather facility
folklore.origin: Apparently a coinage of the Mount Weather folklore layer originating with Richard Pollock, 'The Mysterious Mountain', The Progressive, March 1976. I found no documentary attestation for it in any federal record - though I also did not search federal records for it, which is the check that would settle this.
folklore.why_hollow: STATED AS A HYPOTHESIS WITH A NAMED TEST, NOT A CONCLUSION. The phrase now appears as an alternate official name in the page titles of both the FAS Nuclear Information Project and GlobalSecurity - a T2/T3 source and a T4 source in this project's own tier table. A folklore coinage that has migrated into the nomenclature of reference sites researchers treat as institutional is the laundering pattern CAP-3 exists to catch, and here it is running through the register's own source list. The test is binary and cheap: does the phrase appear in any federal record. If it does, this finding collapses entirely and should be struck.
folklore.mundane_explanation: A journalist's characterising phrase from 1976, repeated without attribution until it acquired the appearance of nomenclature.

folklore.claim: A network of underground federal detention facilities was constructed under REX 84
folklore.origin: The underground element is a 1990s accretion whose own origin I did NOT trace and which remains open. The documented kernel beneath it is real: Alfonso Chardy, Miami Herald, 5 July 1987, and the Brooks-North exchange in the Iran-Contra hearings of 13 July 1987.
folklore.why_hollow: The construction claim leaves no MILCON line, no procurement trace, no NEPA filing, no FRPP entry and no county deed - record classes that sit at X2 and X3 and are not structurally withheld for facilities of this kind. The related 'H.R. 645' item is a real bill, introduced in 2009 and not enacted, concerning above-ground centres on existing military installations; if the legislative record resolves, non-enactment is affirmative documentation of non-funding and an explicit R3 branch. IMPORTANT: the PLANNING half of this claim is not hollow and should not be graded as though it were. The register must split the two, or a real congressional exchange will launder an unevidenced construction claim.
folklore.mundane_explanation: Real Cold War and post-Cold-War federal emergency contingency planning, whose actual products were plans and legal authorities rather than buildings.

silo.claim: Atlas F missile silos have walls almost ten feet thick, made from 'super-hardened, bomb-proof, epoxy-resin concrete', with rebar over three inches thick — making converted silos effectively nuclear-blast-proof homes.
silo.origin: I could not identify the first publication, and I am saying that plainly rather than naming a culprit. What I CAN establish from my sweep: the formulation appears, in near-identical wording, across the silo-real-estate and silo-tourism corpus — a Kansas state tourism blog (travelks.com), a travel blog (getlostintheusa.com), a UK property listicle (loveproperty.com), an Adirondack regional feature, and the missilebases.com/20th Century Castles brokerage material. The wording travels as a unit: 'almost 10 feet thick', 'epoxy resin', 'rebar over three inches'. The most probable origin, on the structure of the corpus and on dating, is 1990s marketing copy from the 20th Century Castles brokerage — the entity that both created this market and wrote its first descriptions — but I did not run the dated negative receipt (Wayback CDX over missilebases.com and the pre-2000 corpus) that an ORIGIN grade requires, so that remains a hypothesis and I have not graded it.
silo.why_hollow: It contradicts an independent technical source in the same sweep. The Federation of American Scientists' Atlas silo description gives the surrounding reinforced-concrete wall as ABOUT 2.5 FEET THICK, and separately notes concrete on the SURFACE at nine feet. The tourism/brokerage version appears to have taken the surface-slab figure and reassigned it to the walls — a transposition, not an invention, which is why it survives casual checking and why it propagates so cleanly. 'Epoxy-resin concrete' is the tell: it is a distinctive, technical-sounding, hard-to-verify detail of exactly the kind that §5.1.7's distinctive-error test identifies as near-dispositive evidence of derivation, because regenerated and paraphrased text loses wording but keeps facts INCLUDING WRONG ONES. The register should treat the presence of 'epoxy resin' in any silo description as a lineage marker rather than as information. Note also the separate 100 psi overpressure figure circulating for Atlas F: that is a plausible design figure for the ORIGINAL structure and is a completely different claim from 'this converted home is blast-proof today'. Fifty years, a sale, and a residential fit-out sit between them.
silo.mundane_explanation: Real hardened Cold War structures, accurately described in one respect (thick concrete somewhere) and inaccurately in another (where), by parties with a commercial interest in the impressive reading, repeated by outlets with no capacity or incentive to check. No fabrication is required at any step. This is the ordinary way a wrong number becomes universal.

silo.claim: The Nekoma pyramid (Stanley R. Mickelsen Safeguard Complex MSR) 'is now a crypto HQ' / is an operating $500 million data centre.
silo.origin: Traceable to a single dated act: the 26 July 2022 announcement from the office of Governor Doug Burgum that Bitzero Blockchain Inc. had signed a binding agreement with the Cavalier County Job Development Authority to acquire the pyramid, with a stated ~$500M expected investment and 35–50 jobs. Within 48 hours the same figures appear across KFYR, Valley News Live, KNOX, Grand Forks Herald, The Center Square, CSi, Walsh County Record, EIN Presswire and DataCenterDynamics. The consumer terminus is the loveproperty/lovemoney gallery headline asserting present-tense operation, syndicated onward through Yahoo. One origin, several dozen copies.
silo.why_hollow: Not fabricated — hollow in the specific sense that the evidence is an ANNOUNCEMENT being reported as an ACCOMPLISHMENT. Against it: Bleeding Heartland raised management and ownership questions in February 2024, and reporting in my sweep indicates that as of November 2024, more than two years on, there was very little evidence of progress at the site and that state funds promised for it had not been used. The only source asserting present operation is a June 2025 PR Newswire release issued by the company itself, which under §2.5 is self-attesting — the author is the claimant and the probative content is the claim — and which describes 2.5MW available at a site announced for 300MW, a two-orders-of-magnitude gap that the headline framing does not survive. Nothing in the citation graph is an interconnection agreement, a permit, an assessment change, or a deed. Under CAP-2b, a FUNCTION claim with no verified instance-scope CLAIM-PROPERTY observation cannot exceed E, and that is the correct disposition. NOTE HONESTLY: this is not a refutation. It is a demonstration that the claim as circulated has no support of the kind that would settle it, and it may yet become true.
silo.mundane_explanation: A02/A07-adjacent: an economic-development announcement with a state political sponsor, a purchase option or staged agreement, and a small pilot deployment sufficient to keep the arrangement alive — reported by a press ecosystem that treats announcements as events. DataCenterDynamics separately reports that at least two earlier attempts to turn Atlas silos in New Mexico into secure data centres or records storage never got off the ground, which is the base rate this claim should have been read against from the start.

silo.claim: Some Colorado Titan I complexes have been 'adapted for alternate use like data storage'.
silo.origin: A single unattributed clause in one enthusiast page (openroadcolorado.com, 'Titan 1 Missile Silos in Colorado'). I found no second source, no named operator, no company, no site, and no date. My targeted follow-up search for a Colorado Titan I data centre returned nothing but the same page, unrelated Titan-named companies, and a stock SEC filing for a firm called Titan Trading Analytics.
silo.why_hollow: It names nothing checkable. A data centre is one of the most externally visible commercial activities that can occupy a building — it needs contracted megawatts, an interconnection, a network presence, customers and usually a marketing website. The expected-record profile for an operating commercial data centre is X2–X3 across utility interconnection, county permits, assessed value and IP-transit route announcements, and NONE of it is present. Under §6.1 this is one of the cases where silence IS informative: absence of evidence for a covert federal facility carries nearly no information, but absence of evidence for a commercial data centre carries a great deal, because a commercial data centre has every incentive to be findable. This is the register's own asymmetry rule doing useful work in the direction people forget it runs.
silo.mundane_explanation: Almost certainly a garbled recollection of the well-documented general phenomenon of underground facilities being used for records storage and data centres — Iron Mountain at Boyers, the Kansas City limestone complexes — attached loosely to Colorado Titan I sites, which are in fact largely flooded, hazardous and under state environmental oversight for solvent contamination. The competing description in the SAME sweep — a 2024 county rescue operation inside a silo headlined 'Death around every corner' — is hard to reconcile with an operating data centre and is much better sourced.

silo.claim: Decommissioned Atlas/Titan/Nike sites are entrances or nodes in a national network of deep underground military bases, connected by tunnels.
silo.origin: The DUMB corpus, whose modern American form traces to a small self-published 1990s origin set — the Sauder/Schneider '129 deep underground military bases' material, which the calibration suite carries at F-03. In my own sweep the query surfaced deepundergroundmilitarybases.com and a silo.tips PDF host of 'Secret Underground Bases', which is the same corpus recirculating. Nothing in it originates on this beat; the missile-silo attachment is an accretion onto a claim structure that predates it.
silo.why_hollow: Missile fields are the single worst possible substrate for this claim, and that is the interesting part. This is the most extensively surveyed, most thoroughly declassified, most completely disposed-of category of hardened American infrastructure that exists: Air Force site lists, GSA auction records, county deeds for every parcel, FUDS property records, state environmental files, NRHP nominations, HAER measured drawings, squadron veterans' associations publishing site-by-site histories, and — for the Minuteman population — a bilateral treaty verification regime under which an ADVERSARY GOVERNMENT was invited to confirm by satellite that each launcher had been destroyed and the hole left open for ninety days. The expected-record profile for a tunnel network connecting these sites would be X3 on spoil-volume accounting, X3 on construction procurement, X3 on county land records for the intervening right-of-way, and X3 on the treaty inventories. That silence is loudly informative. But §8.4 forbids R on negatives alone, and this claim earns F — SILENCE-DOMINATED, with V empty via §2.5, exactly as F-03 does. I want to be precise about the direction: the register is not saying 'no tunnels because we found nothing'. It is saying the claim has no verified support of any kind, and separately that the records which would exist do not.
silo.mundane_explanation: A12/A11: real, individually documented, individually disposed-of military facilities of a known typology, aggregated into an imagined system by a corpus that predates and is indifferent to their actual records. The tunnels that genuinely exist — the cableways and utility tunnels between a Titan I silo and its control dome, the tunnel junctions of a Titan II complex — are real, documented, short, and connect a site to itself.

silo.claim: Individual former Minuteman launch facilities in the Grand Forks field survive as intact hardened structures available for purchase and conversion.
silo.origin: A conflation of two true things: (a) GSA did auction former 321st Missile Wing parcels to private buyers, with reported bids from about $6,000 to $17,800, reported by the Grand Forks Herald; and (b) former missile properties generally are bought and converted, which is true of Atlas and Titan sites and of Minuteman MISSILE ALERT FACILITIES. The conflation runs through the general silo-real-estate corpus rather than through any single identifiable source.
silo.why_hollow: The Minuteman LAUNCH FACILITIES in this population were destroyed before disposal, by treaty requirement — controlled explosive demolition with roughly 800 lb of explosives, the excavation left open for ninety days for verification. What was auctioned is in most cases the parcel and its surface remnants, not a usable subsurface structure. The two classes of property — a launch control facility with its intact underground capsule, and a launch facility with a demolished and backfilled duct — are routinely spoken of together as 'missile sites for sale' and are physically nothing alike. Recorded here because it is a live consumer-facing error rather than a fringe one: someone can lose money on it. The discriminating documents are the START elimination notifications and the GSA disposal descriptions, both enumerable.
silo.mundane_explanation: Two accurate facts about the same real estate market, describing two different asset classes, merged by imprecise category language. No one had to be wrong on purpose.

silo.claim: The Adirondack Atlas F silo at Lewis, New York (556-5) houses a cosmic-ray / low-background detection facility for SUNY Plattsburgh researchers.
silo.origin: One Adirondack Explorer feature ('Disco, Stout and Cosmic Rays'), whose headline itself implies three separate silo afterlives across the twelve-site Plattsburgh ring. In the summary I received, the cosmic-ray use was attributed to 'Site 5 in Lewis' in one sentence while the article's broader subject includes the Au Sable Forks site 556-6.
silo.why_hollow: Recorded as UNRESOLVED rather than refuted, and I want the distinction preserved. The underlying activity is entirely plausible — a deep rock-cut void with low ambient background is genuinely attractive for low-background counting, and the physics literature contains many such shallow-underground facilities. What is missing is any second source: no publication, no technical report, no institutional record, no equipment-siting document names an Adirondack missile silo as a counting location. My targeted search returned only Gran Sasso, Felsenkeller, Dortmund and Argonne. Until a paper or an institutional record names the site, this is a magazine sentence, its site attribution is ambiguous between two silos twelve miles apart, and it should not be attached to either entry as a FEATURE. Flagged as a lead worth two minutes of a literature search once egress works.
silo.mundane_explanation: A06 — an underground space used for ordinary purposes, to which a research use is loosely or retrospectively attached; or a real but small and undocumented university project; or a correct fact attached to the wrong one of twelve nearly identical sites. All three are ordinary and none require anyone to have said anything false.

coverage_gaps_carried_forward.cog: WHAT I DID NOT COVER, AND WHY. (1) The Greenbrier / Project Greek Island is absent from the candidate list although I searched it and confirmed the anchor facts (Ted Gup, Washington Post, 31 May 1992; construction 1959-62 alongside the West Virginia Wing; the Forsythe Associates cover). It is calibration case B-05/A-05 and I could add nothing to it under snippet-only retrieval. Same for Mount Weather as an entity, though its 'underground city' claim is worked in refuted_or_hollow, and same for Cheyenne Mountain. (2) The remaining PEF sites — Cartwheel at Fort Reno Park in the District of Columbia, Cannonball at Cross Mountain near Mercersburg Pennsylvania, Cowpuncher at Martinsburg West Virginia, Cadre/Creed near Site R, Cactus, and Crystal at Mount Weather — are each identified with a location and a site number but I worked up only Corkscrew. Cartwheel is the most interesting omission because it is calibration case B-03, sits under a public city park, and turns on whether White House Army Signal Agency records name Fort Reno at instance or only at class level. (3) The eight-region enumeration's own source. I saw the list; I never reached the NARA Guide pages for RG 304, 396, 397 or 311 that appear to carry it. Everything structural in this file rests on that unverified list and a downstream process should treat it as a single unresolved lineage, not as a finding aid. (4) Departmental emergency relocation sites beyond Front Royal. If roughly 90 arc sites existed, I have touched one, and the college-campus sites mentioned in passing by the arc literature are entirely unexamined. This is the largest recall gap in the beat and probably the richest remaining seam. (5) State-level emergency operating centres, which are numerous, frequently hardened, and documented in state rather than federal records — an entirely unworked corpus that is also unusually reachable, since state archives and state emergency-management agencies publish. (6) Post-1980s and post-9/11 continuity architecture. I touched Peters Mountain, Albemarle County Virginia — an AT&T troposcatter and long-lines site reported as nuclear-hardened, reported to house several hundred people, and reported to have had a renovation exceeding $61 million since 2007 — but did not develop it, and it is the strongest live COG candidate I did not work up. It also sits at the intersection of this beat and the AT&T Long Lines beat and should be coordinated rather than duplicated. (7) The Federal Preparedness Agency inheritance within GSA (NARA RG 269) was named in my brief and I did not reach it at all. (8) HERT, the Headquarters Emergency Relocation Team, surfaced as a SAC continuity unit at Offutt AFB with a dispersal location at the Cornhusker Army Ammunition Plant, Grand Island, Nebraska, superseded circa 1982 by the Enduring Battle Management Support Center. I excluded it because it is a UNIT rather than a structure and carries no hardened-facility claim, but the dispersal locations it used are unexamined and are exactly the sort of unglamorous COG geography this beat is supposed to find. (9) MOST IMPORTANTLY: no canonical corpus was searched in the BES 7.1 sense. Zero queries against CREST, DTIC, NARA Catalog, GovInfo, the Federal Register, FRUS, GAO, MILCON J-books, NEPA repositories, FRPP, the DoD Base Structure Report, USAspending/FPDS, county recorders or the USGS historical topographic stack. SCI is therefore approximately zero across this entire beat and no negative finding anywhere in this file is a NEGATIVE — every one of them is UNSEARCHED. Nothing here should be read as evidence of absence, and the several places where I say 'I searched for undercutting evidence and found none' should be read as statements about my reach, not about the world.
coverage_gaps_carried_forward.comms:
WHAT THIS SWEEP DID NOT TOUCH, in rough order of how much it matters.

1. EVERY CANONICAL CORPUS. No FCC ASR or ULS, no county recorder or assessor in any of the eleven counties named above, no USGS HTMC temporal stack, no GovInfo, no NARA, no CREST, no DTIC, no AFHRA, no FRPP, no GSA disposal. This is not a prioritisation choice; the hosts are unreachable. It means the beat's central promise — that FCC registrations and infrastructure records give it real documentary anchors — is entirely unredeemed by this cycle. The anchors were identified; none was pulled.

2. THE WESTERN UNION SIDE OF THE HOUSE. The literature is overwhelmingly AT&T-shaped. Western Union ran a parallel hardened government microwave network including the Washington Area Wideband System, with named nodes at the Naval Security Station, NSA's Friendship Annex, Andrews AFB, Liberty Dam and the Alternate Joint Communications Center. I found the system's name, an acronym that will index well in federal corpora, a route map, and a peer-reviewed scholarly treatment of the company's microwave programme (Rotenstein 2006) — and I searched none of the federal corpora for 'WAWS'. This is the largest unexplored seam I found and I would rank it first for the next cycle.

3. AUTOVON AS A SYSTEM. Reports of 'at least 38' hardened switching centres circulate; I developed one (Pottstown PA) barely and named Cheshire CT and Monrovia MD without developing them at all. AUTOVON has a published architecture, a documented DCA lineage and a finite switch list, which makes it a far more tractable candidate-set target than 'Project Offices'. A full enumeration of the AUTOVON switch list against county records would be a productive dedicated cycle.

4. THE L-CARRIER BURIED PLANT. Roughly a thousand hardened repeater vaults were built along the L-3I and L-4 routes — concrete vaults under small surface huts at roughly four-mile spacing along continuous cross-country rights of way. These are the most numerous hardened structures in the United States and are almost entirely unregistered anywhere. They are also, individually, near-worthless as candidates and collectively very valuable as a mapped route. The right treatment is a route geometry with a PROGRAM proposition, not a thousand entries, and I did not attempt it.

5. FEDERAL SPECTRUM. As the source registry states, the networks that actually served continuity-of-government facilities were licensed through NTIA/IRAC and are absent from the FCC record by construction. Everything findable on this beat is the commercial shadow of an invisible federal system. The register should state this on every comms entry rather than treating FCC silence as meaningful.

6. THE FUNDING QUESTION. Whether the AT&T Project Offices were built with AT&T capital, with federal money, or on a cost-shared basis is the single fact that would most reorganise this beat — it determines whether MILCON, DD-1391 and FPDS profiles are X0 or X3, and therefore whether the documentary silence around these five stations is uninformative or damning. I could not establish it and I do not think anyone in the open literature has.

7. ORIGIN WORK PROPER. No Wayback CDX sweep, no IA full-text hits_inside, no Chronicling America or Open ONI search of construction-era local press in Chatham, Buckingham, Washington, Albemarle, Loudoun, Burt, Boone, Morris or Hampshire counties. Every claim-origin trace in this file is therefore an EARLIEST APPEARANCE I HAPPENED TO FIND, not a receipted earliest appearance, and no ORIGIN proposition is offered anywhere in this file for that reason. Note specifically that the 1960s construction-era local press for most of these sites falls after 1963, which is where Chronicling America's free corpus stops for copyright reasons — a real, specific, structural archive gap that will need a paid database.

8. AT&T'S OWN CORPORATE RECORD. Bell System Practices, Bell Laboratories Record articles, Long Lines route and plant engineering literature, and the AT&T Archives. Per the calibration set, this is the class of document that carries D3 for hardening claims on this typology, and it is the class that would collapse a dozen compiler-dependent propositions into properly sourced ones at a stroke. The archives.long-lines.com mirror of L4 documentation and the qsl.net transcription are both pointers into it and neither was followed.

9. GEOLOCATION. Zero coordinates resolved, deliberately (see method_notes). Every candidate needs a parcel or ASR pull before it can carry a LOCATE proposition at any band, and several are trivially obtainable — the Lyons site has a published street address and a registered 329-foot tower; the Missouri repeaters have ASR numbers with surveyed coordinates.
coverage_gaps_carried_forward.folklore:
THE PRIORITY HARVEST QUEUE, in the order I would fetch it. Each of these is a specific document that would move a specific proposition, and every one is free and outside the classification system:
1. https://cdnc.ucr.edu/?a=d&d=SPNP19340130.2.36 - San Pedro News Pilot, 30 January 1934. Would ground the cleanest ORIGIN entry on the beat. FETCH-BLOCKED here.
2. https://www.loc.gov/item/oh1655 and the HAER OH-79-AN photographic set - would refute the 'Hangar 18' identity claim from a T1 survey. FETCH-BLOCKED here.
3. https://archives.denverlibrary.org/repositories/3/resources/6538 - the New World Airport Commission finding aid. FETCH-BLOCKED here.
4. https://www.osti.gov/servlets/purl/4444905 (LA-5354-MS) and https://www.osti.gov/servlets/purl/4687637 (LA-4547) - would establish the subterrene PROGRAM proposition at a real band.
5. US Patent 3,693,731 at the USPTO's own interface, not an aggregator - forgery pricing under BES A6 requires the issuing authority.
6. Kittitas County Assessor and Auditor property records for any owner named Waters, late 1990s - the single record that decides whether Mel's Hole is R or F.
7. New York Times Book Review, 19 March 1972 - Lewin's admission, the beat's cleanest R1.
8. Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors minutes, 21 February 1933 - the Shufelt excavation contract.
9. Iran-Contra hearing transcript, 13 July 1987 - pre-1994 congressional material is scanned-only in GovInfo, so this is an acquisition task, not a search. Flag ARCHIVE-GAP.
10. California Mining Journal, November 1940 - the Dorr affidavit as first published, plus a collation against the 10 December 1934 variant.

WHAT THIS BEAT STILL HAS NOT DONE, AND IT IS THE MAIN THING. Not one negative receipt was logged. Every ORIGIN proposition in this file is therefore a statement about where a claim is FOUND rather than where it ORIGINATES, and the register should not publish them as origins until the canonical ORIGIN set has been run: Wayback CDX with collapse=digest, IA full-text hits_inside, the AFU 'ufonewsletters' collection, UTZOO Usenet, textfiles.com, Arctic Shift, Chronicling America and Open ONI. The single highest-value unrun search on the whole beat is the pre-1995 check on the strings '1,477' and '129 underground bases', which the register's own source registry already flags as unverified.

OPEN THREADS I DID NOT CLOSE. (a) The origin of the UNDERGROUND element of the FEMA-camps claim - I traced the political kernel to 1987 and the underground accretion to nobody. (b) Whether the 1980 film 'Hangar 18' created the nomenclature it appears to describe, which would be a textbook citogenesis event. (c) Whether the 1990s DUMB corpus descends from Shaver 1945 by citation or merely resembles it - the concrete handle is the reported LeVesque connection to Shaver Mystery material, which would link the 1945 template to the 1989 Dulce text through one identified person. (d) Whether 'Western Virginia Office of Controlled Conflict Operations' appears in any federal record.

A STRUCTURAL GAP IN THE RUBRIC ITSELF, offered for consideration rather than as a finding. The expected-record framework is built for facilities where concealment is the controlling variable and silence is routine. Two entries here invert that: at Kokoweef and at Fort Moore Hill, the searchers were the PROPONENTS, funded, motivated, with lawful access, digging at the claimed location - for ninety years in one case. Their failure is signed evidence of a different and much stronger kind than a missing MILCON line, and there is no ERP profile for it. I would propose a 'proponent-searchable claim' profile where a sustained, funded, on-site negative by the claimant's own party scores as affirmative UNDERCUTS rather than as documentary absence, which would let those two entries reach R by a legitimate route instead of resting at F.

WHAT I DELIBERATELY DID NOT DO. I did not manufacture coordinates. Six of the twelve entries carry precision 'none' or 'claimed-only' and no lat/lon, because the claims themselves have never been located, and a precise pin manufactured from imprecise evidence would be the register performing its own citogenesis at the interface layer. I also declined to close Wright-Patterson EXIST, which is genuinely unresolved from open records, rather than grade it to look decisive.
coverage_gaps_carried_forward.silo:
WHAT I DID NOT COVER, ranked by how much it costs the register.

1. THE ENTIRE CANONICAL SOURCE SET. Not one index was enumerated. No NARA catalog API walk of RG 77 / RG 341 / RG 342 by ancestorNaId; no DTIC search by originating lab report series (AFWL-TR, AFSWC-TR, DASA, DNA-TR, WES) which SOURCE-REGISTRY identifies as the richest corpus for hardened-structure engineering and which would settle nearly every HARDEN proposition in this file; no FUDS FeatureServer sweep filtered on Nike/Titan/Atlas/Minuteman property names, which is described as the best single geospatial source for decommissioned hardened infrastructure and which alone would produce hundreds of instance candidates with durable FUDS property-number join keys; no GSA disposal records; no county recorder queries anywhere; no NPGallery full-text search of NRHP nominations for 'blast door', 'hardened', 'shock isolation'; no USGS HTMC temporal stacks; no FCC ASR; no Chronicling America or state newspaper programs (Colorado Historic Newspapers, Wyoming, Nevada, New Mexico and Utah matter disproportionately here); no AAFM newsletter run or 'Taps for Missileers'; no Wayback CDX. Every one of these was blocked or unreachable. This is not a research plan I chose; it is the entire methodology of the register, unavailable.

2. WHOLE PROGRAMS ABSENT. Titan I in Washington (568th SMS, Larson AFB — I surfaced but did not develop a complex at Royal City/Quincy reported as flooded and used for technical diving, which is a genuinely unusual afterlife worth an entry); Titan I in Idaho, California and South Dakota; the Atlas E rings at Forbes, Fairchild and Lincoln beyond the single Kansas conversion; the entire Nike population outside two Maryland sites — roughly 250 defended-area sites nationally, with Ed Thelen's register as the ready-made enumeration and an acute succession risk attached to it (he died in 2024; SOURCE-REGISTRY says mirror it now, and I endorse that as urgent); Safeguard's Missile Site Radar remote launch sites RSL-1, RSL-2 and RSL-4; the Nike Zeus and Sprint/Spartan test infrastructure at Kwajalein and White Sands; Minuteman at Whiteman, Ellsworth and Malmstrom; Peacekeeper/MX basing including the Deep Basing and Closely Spaced Basing studies, which are a PROGRAM-class opportunity of the DUCC shape — heavily documented, never built, and currently unrepresented.

3. NIKE W-25, DAVIDSONVILLE, MARYLAND — deliberately left as a partial. It is now the Anne Arundel County Police Training Academy, it has a Maryland Department of the Environment Voluntary Cleanup Program document (a state regulator describing a former launch and control site for its own purposes), and it has a named scholarly monograph (Merle T. Cole's 'W-25: The Davidsonville Site and Maryland Air Defense, 1950–1974'). That combination — regulator plus scholar plus county reuse — is a stronger evidentiary structure than several candidates I did develop, and it should be first in the next cycle.

4. THE CONVERSION-FAILURE POPULATION. DataCenterDynamics reports at least two failed attempts to make New Mexico Atlas silos into secure data centres or records storage. Failed conversions are systematically absent from the corpus because nobody writes about a thing that did not happen, and they are exactly what the register should collect: they establish the base rate against which every announced conversion — Nekoma included — must be read. There is no index of them. Building one is a genuine contribution and would have to be done by working GSA disposal records and county deeds forward, not by searching.

5. NO SIGNED NEGATIVES. I produced no receipted negative searches. Every absence in this file is UNSEARCHED, not NEGATIVE, and per §6.2 an unsearched record class produces NO ROW — not a zero. Nothing here may be scored against any candidate as an absence.

6. THE ONE THING I MOST WANT THE NEXT CYCLE TO INHERIT. For this beat the register's default epistemic posture should be INVERTED relative to the COG beats. These programs were publicly appropriated, publicly built, publicly disposed of and in the Minuteman case adversarially verified. Missing records here are surprising, and the expected-record tables should carry a silo/launch-facility profile that says so explicitly, rather than defaulting to the classified-facility charity that is correct for Greenbrier-in-1991 and wrong for an Atlas F in Cloud County.
